# 50 super successful college dropouts

 By Joal Ryan

March 18, 2021 / 3:15 PM EDT / CBS News

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

![Image 4: 2018 MoMA David Rockefeller Award Luncheon Honoring Oprah Winfrey ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/8f488567-13ec-4afa-ba12-e5b8d2c446ce/thumbnail/620x372/74847a6a9f75bd90fa3e4de4193d8f6a/dropouts-oprah.jpg#)

 Gonzalo Marroquin/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images 

For many, college provides a road to success. But it's not the only road. Here's a look at dozens of tech, business, political and media stars of the 20th century and beyond who left school without undergrad degrees, but with plenty of ambition and talent to make things happen.

First up: [Oprah Winfrey](https://www.cbsnews.com/video/oprah-winfrey-on-her-bombshell-harry-and-meghan-interview/).

In 1975, the future media mogul and philanthropist left Tennessee State University for a TV job one credit shy of completing her four-year degree. A decade later, after launching her talk show and earning an Oscar nomination, Winfrey resumed her studies. She graduated as a member of Tennessee State's Class of 1986.

## Steve Jobs

![Image 5: T-Mobile Gets iPhone Germany Contract ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/d9a05f7f-cd28-4588-9f32-2a5df65155c8/thumbnail/620x372/6014e3fdc8aefaa43706effd7af3b43e/dropouts-jobs.jpg#)

 Sean Gallup/Getty Images 

The Apple co-founder "may ... be one of the most famous dropouts in history," per [Reed College](https://www.reed.edu/steve-jobs.html#:~:text=As%20everyone%20knows%2C%20Steve%20Jobs,%2C%20but%20didn't%20graduate.&text=Questioning%20everything%20and%20everyone%2C%20Steve,designing%20the%20revolutionary%20Apple%20Macintosh.), the liberal arts school in Oregon which [Steve Jobs](https://www.cbsnews.com/feature/steve-jobs-1955-2011/) left after just one semester. ("I ran out of money," Jobs [explained](https://www.reed.edu/reed-magazine/articles/2018/steve-jobs-staying-hungry.html) in a 1991 commencement speech at the school.)

## Mark Zuckerberg

![Image 6: Facebook Founder Mark Zuckerberg Delivers Commencement Address At Harvard ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/e70f1918-e28a-42a1-a1e3-2a08b4ce0a7e/thumbnail/620x372/7426fdf0fa500c905836f358ba5bea81/dropouts-zuckerberg.jpg#)

 Paul Marotta/Getty Images 

In 2017, the Facebook CEO was a commencement speaker at Harvard University. [Mark Zuckerberg](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/facebook-ceo-mark-zuckerberg-wife-priscilla-chan-inside-their-home-family-life/) dropped out of the Ivy League school in 2005 to focus on his then-young but growing social media platform.

## Alicia Keys

![Image 7: 62nd Annual GRAMMY Awards - Show ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/3567dcfd-c05e-415e-8c57-31d498dd126d/thumbnail/620x372/7ad0bdc8597a9528429bcbb30da80e5f/dropouts-keys.jpg#)

 Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic/Getty Images 

In the late 1990s, according to an Oprah magazine [interview with singer-songwriter Alicia Keys](https://www.oprah.com/omagazine/oprahs-interview-with-alicia-keys), the future Grammy-winner left Columbia University after four weeks for a music deal with Columbia Records. She was all of 16 at the time.

## Dick Cheney

![Image 8: Dick Cheney Made a Statement ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/dc64545d-2401-4469-8271-f7054d1ea320/thumbnail/620x372/d377823c38201aa00c0ce3cc2426ea2f/dropouts-cheney.jpg#)

 Alex Wong/Newsmakers/Getty Images 

According to the [Yale Daily News](https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2003/09/19/famous-failures/), [Dick Cheney](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/never-before-seen-photos-of-bush-administration-during-9-11/11/) dropped out of the Ivy League school _twice_. (Biography.com and other sources describe the departures as Cheney having "[failed out](https://www.biography.com/news/dick-cheney-political-rise-vice-president).")

The future U.S. vice president would eventually settle into higher education and earn bachelor's and master's degrees at the University of Wyoming.

## Joel Osteen

![Image 9: Today - Season 62 ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/2ad58c54-ff60-44eb-aef5-7e0266dd06e4/thumbnail/620x372/6ad048405b81bfa0910ab9fab133b586/dropouts-osteen.jpg#)

 Peter Kramer/NBC/NBC Newswire/NBCUniversal/Getty Images 

[Joel Osteen](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/the-positivity-of-joel-osteen/)dropped out of Oral Roberts University as a freshman in the early 1980s. The pastor went on to help build his father's Houston evangelical church, Lakewood, into the [biggest megachurch in the United States](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/30-biggest-american-megachurches-ranked/30/), with about 43,500 weekly visitors in pre-COVID times.

## Tiger Woods

![Image 10: California v Stanford ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/68c3d28d-702e-4d31-97c8-a079d320da16/thumbnail/620x372/5b38f929e04d5306422adda6d426bd69/dropouts-woods.jpg#)

 Ezra Shaw/Getty Images 

Like many elite athletes, Tiger Woods left college early to pursue his sport professionally. In his case, he exited Stanford after his sophomore year. "[T]he only regret I have in life is not spending another year at Stanford," Woods [said](https://golf.com/news/tiger-woods-reveals-his-greatest-regret-to-charlie-rose/) in 2016.

## Bill Gates

![Image 11: Microsoft Co-founder Bill Gates ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/daf667f2-5b97-4631-9934-670467ca2f7f/thumbnail/620x372/895fed25400967c490e84acb4d2c932f/dropouts-gates.jpg#)

 Doug Wilson/CORBIS/Corbis/Getty Images 

The future philanthropist [left Harvard](https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2013/09/dawn-of-a-revolution/) after the end of his sophomore year. He would return, but drop out for good after completing his junior year. Both times, [Bill Gates](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bill-gates-climate-change-disaster-60-minutes-2021-02-14/) exited school to focus on the company he co-founded in 1975: Microsoft.

## Brad Pitt

![Image 12: 86th Annual Academy Awards - Arrivals ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/32f40097-a774-4fb5-87f4-7fb321c726b8/thumbnail/620x372/c2c0e6addb0dd911d95e54fc8b9df16e/dropouts-pitt.jpg#)

 Jeff Vespa/WireImage/Getty Images 

Oscar-winning actor and producer Brad Pitt is the college dropout who almost wasn't. He told "Fresh Air" that he left the University of Missouri for Los Angeles just two weeks shy of graduation. "I just felt I was done," the former journalism major [explained](https://www.poynter.org/reporting-editing/2011/why-brad-pitt-dropped-out-of-missouri-journalism-school/). "I was done with it. I knew where I wanted to go."

## Rachael Ray

![Image 13: Food Network & Cooking Channel New York City Wine & Food Festival presented by Capital One - Grand Tasting presented by ShopRite featuring Culinary Demonstrations at The IKEA Kitchen presented by Capital One ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/938368ca-b3b2-47a2-84b6-262e7c5591d2/thumbnail/620x372/a608905cd9d4590f1d6400ea97665d3d/dropouts-ray.jpg#)

 John Lamparski/Getty Images for NYCWFF 

Future[TV talk show host](https://www.rachaelrayshow.com/) and Food Network star Rachael Ray dropped out of New York's Pace University after two years, she [told](https://www.vanityfair.com/culture/2007/10/rachaelray200710) Vanity Fair, because her tuition was pricey —and "it was more like I was going to school for hobbies." Her next move? Taking a job at the candy counter at Macy's.

## Jack Dorsey

![Image 14: Square And Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey Speaks At Empowering Entrepreneurs Event ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/ec56c8c2-ec2f-4c41-81eb-3449bcbf4f56/thumbnail/620x372/3cd73ce45891aa760796395f949b2dc2/dropouts-dorsey.jpg#)

 Cole Burston/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

Jack Dorsey, the co-founder of Twitter and Square, dropped out of college twice. According to a [New Yorker profile](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2013/10/21/two-hit-wonder), Dorsey left Missouri University of Science and Technology in his junior year for a job in New York, and then exited New York University just shy of graduation for a short-lived West Coast venture. "I felt like a failure," Dorsey would recall of his mid-20s self.

## Daniel Ek

![Image 15: Attendees Arrive For Allen & Co. Media And Technology Conference ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/a230d97f-b81f-4b83-9f2d-7e2d53e7a041/thumbnail/620x372/f9f36c5c19d69402c6ebb490fc469ab2/dropouts-ek.jpg#)

 Patrick T. Fallon/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

[Daniel Ek](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spotify-ipo-music-streaming-startup-hopes-stock-offering-is-a-smash-hit/)is the CEO and founder of Spotify. According to a [Forbes profile on the streaming mogul](https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevenbertoni/2012/01/04/spotifys-daniel-ek-the-most-important-man-in-music/?sh=24d97ed864ca), Ek dropped out of Sweden's Royal Institute of Technology after just eight weeks.

## Ellen DeGeneres

![Image 16: 86th Annual Academy Awards - Show ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/ac5a03d7-60e4-4705-a7d6-fdfcf451a8f6/thumbnail/620x372/794a36c871430e27afa471c63f2cea1a/dropouts-ellen.jpg#)

 Kevin Winter/Getty Images 

Ellen DeGeneres dropped out of the University of New Orleans after "less than a semester," [Parade noted](https://parade.com/482237/dotsonrader/ellen-degeneres-talks-feelings-fun-and-finding-dory/). "School was just not interesting to me," she told the outlet. DeGeneres went on to find her way in stand-up comedy, sitcoms, TV talk shows and Oscar-hosting duties.

## Ashton Kutcher

![Image 17: WeWork Presents Second Annual Creator Global Finals At Microsoft Theater ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/2c8e7c6f-a339-4ef4-bfc8-4190e653b08e/thumbnail/620x372/3cd31a37fb617c79009d08a644e9fbfa/dropouts-kutcher.jpg#)

 Michael Kovac/Getty Images for WeWork 

In the late 1990s, Ashton Kutcher was studying biochemical engineering at the University of Iowa when he dropped out to pursue modeling. The decision ultimately put him on the path to becoming an actor and tech investor.

"I pursued something I was passionate about and … I haven't felt like I've worked a day even though I work every day," Kutcher [told](https://www.newsweek.com/college-credit-ashton-kutcher-going-broke-university-education-1465142) Newsweek of leaving college. "So, that was the right decision for me."

## Quincy Jones

![Image 18: Quincy Jones has written a new book that arrives on the heels of 2 retrospective CD releases. He is ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/cc6a5b65-dfb9-4755-a162-201d627e0280/thumbnail/620x372/e0475e6e8be9dc4b5622954faf80c1f7/dropouts-jones.jpg#)

 Lawrence K. Ho/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images 

When the teenaged Quincy Jones left the Berklee College of Music to take a gig with jazz great Lionel Hampton, he told the school he intended to return. "[B]ut I guess down inside ... when you go with a band like that you never go back," the music legend [told](https://www.npr.org/2013/05/27/186052477/quincy-jones-the-man-behind-the-music) NPR.

## Ralph Lauren

![Image 19: Fashion designer Ralph Lauren receives applause fr ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/f59962a0-3a92-4b1d-b249-120ee3bfc570/thumbnail/620x372/db605a6fa01058b09b9013c61b11fbda/dropouts-lauren2.jpg#)

 JON LEVY/AFP/Getty Images 

By Ralph Lauren's [own bio](https://corporate.ralphlauren.com/leadership-ralph-lauren-full-bio.html), the future designer and founder of the famous Polo brand dropped out of New York City's Baruch College after two years to enlist in the U.S. Army.

## Steven Spielberg

![Image 20: Steven Spielberg Holding Two Oscars ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/b6ecfa28-82af-425d-a94c-5edc4bca42df/thumbnail/620x372/92f91a6b846022bbc8debc1e21d19c7a/dropouts-spielberg.jpg#)

 Steve Starr/CORBIS/Corbis/Getty Images 

[Steven Spielberg](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/steven-spielberg-alex-gibney-why-we-hate-docuseries/)dropped out of Cal State Long Beach in the late 1960s [to direct for TV](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/steven-spielberg-sidney-sheinberg-59773). After winning three Oscars, the blockbuster filmmaker resumed his studies, and [earned his bachelor's degree at Long Beach in 2002](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-may-31-me-graduate31-story.html).

## Kat Cole

![Image 21: Cosmopolitan Fun Fearless Money 2016 ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/a8d8464f-45a9-40a6-a489-285cf8b5ab7a/thumbnail/620x372/a137f44d6034686cbf819ed437809dab/dropouts-cole.jpg#)

 Cindy Ord/Getty Images for Cosmopolitan 

Kat Cole is the former president of Focus Brands, the parent company of Cinnabon, Auntie Anne's and more. She dropped out of the University of North Florida at age 20 because she was [finding it difficult to juggle studies with her growing responsibilities](https://www.northwesternmutual.com/life-and-money/how-kat-cole-went-from-college-dropout-to-president-of-a-global-brand/) at Hooters, the restaurant chain where she'd begun working as a teenager.

Cole is a different kind of dropout on this list because while she never earned a bachelor's degree, she [does hold an MBA](https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/227970).She pursued the graduate degree after becoming a Hooters vice president in her mid-20s.

## Vin Diesel

![Image 22: One Voice: Somos Live! A Concert For Disaster Relief - Miami ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/0b680700-4673-4552-a402-35513005f6bd/thumbnail/620x372/f8b8e58d1aaaa02840148a28f1c850a2/dropouts-diesel.jpg#)

 Rick Diamond/One Voice: Somos Live!/Getty Images 

According to Hunter College, future box-office star Vin Diesel [was an English major](http://www.hunter.cuny.edu/communications/pressroom/news/actor-vin-diesel-to-deliver-commencement-address-and-receive-honorary-degree-at-hunter-colleges-spring-2018-graduation-ceremony-on-may-30) at the New York campus in the late 1980s. He left school to pursue acting.

## David Neeleman

![Image 23: JetBlue CEO David Neeleman near Airplanes ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/5bfecc43-6935-4ac4-8729-6c56a815b820/thumbnail/620x372/4afee14bb07aec31dd011d611d1f2d63/dropouts-neeleman.jpg#)

 Mark Peterson/Corbis/Getty Images 

Asked by the San Francisco Chronicle where he went to school, JetBlue Airways founder David Neeleman [put it succinctly](https://www.sfgate.com/business/ontherecord/article/ON-THE-RECORD-DAVID-NEELEMAN-Jetblue-Airways-2694430.php): "University of Utah. But I dropped out." Neeleman said a Mormon missionary experience in Brazil broadened his horizons; the "A" student would leave school to start his own travel business.

## Sofia Vergara

![Image 24: 2020 Vanity Fair Oscar Party Hosted By Radhika Jones - Arrivals ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/4caf905e-536c-48cc-a75e-55280324f224/thumbnail/620x372/c73a0089a955950a31b8b31a509e2f67/dropouts-vergara.jpg#)

 Toni Anne Barson/WireImage/Getty images 

Now famous for flashing her smile on the red carpet, Sofia Vergara studied dentistry in college in her native Columbia. "But I didn't finish," the "Modern Family" star [said](https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/sofia-vergara-d-d-s-modern-family-star-says-she-studied-dentistry-before-acting) in a 2016 talk-show appearance.

## William McKinley

![Image 25: Portrait of President William McKinley ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7fe517b6-4cc2-4f48-bda2-d0fc9358c19b/thumbnail/620x372/9aa820fcf7252f7ebc17652f597dff80/dropouts-mckinley.jpg#)

 Oscar White/Corbis/VCG/Getty Images 

President William McKinley is one of only two college dropouts to serve in the 20th century White House.

[According to Pennsvlvania's Allegheny College](https://sites.allegheny.edu/about/history/stories/), which McKinley attended, it's not known why the future U.S. president didn't complete his degree. The school says McKinley called his lack of a diploma "one of the greatest regrets of his life."

## Kanye West

![Image 26: US rapper Kanye West holds his three Gra ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/d6514092-805c-42de-bc8d-99ac77c19193/thumbnail/620x372/7d56cf560bbf22d089d58a756557f2af/dropouts-kanye.jpg#)

 ROBYN BECK/AFP/Getty Images 

The future rap and Yeezy mogul attended both the American Academy of Art and Chicago State University, but he graduated from neither. In the end, West earned a batch of Grammy Awards for his 2004 album, "The College Dropout."

## Madonna

![Image 27: Madonna Performs In Minnesota ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/06d1f5b5-0878-4657-b9ba-be971c775bd7/thumbnail/620x372/bc6f0c1472a4518529756839c2090c71/dropouts-madonna.jpg#)

 Jim Steinfeldt/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images 

[Madonna](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/madonna/8/)called herself a "famed high-school dropout" in a [1983 "American Bandstand" interview](https://youtu.be/TfvkofbxlOA)with Dick Clark, but she's actually a _college_ dropout: According to the University of Michigan, the pop icon studied at the Big Ten school for two years before moving to New York —and into the spotlight.

## R. Donahue Peebles

![Image 28: Key Speakers At The 2017 Milken Conference ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/991d08a0-11bb-4bf0-83cd-63c75057f931/thumbnail/620x372/a29c7b8e7dc8ae3d5afaf7e7efcc7506/dropouts-peebles.jpg#)

 Patrick T. Fallon/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

In 2015, a few years after including R. Donahue Peebles on its list of the [wealthiest Black Americans](https://webcache.googleusercontent.com/search?q=cache:2HNJbJS52z4J:https://www.forbes.com/2009/05/06/richest-black-americans-busienss-billionaires-richest-black-americans.html+&cd=6&hl=en&ct=clnk&gl=us), Forbes pegged the real estate developer's net worth at [more than $700 million](https://webcache.googleusercontent.com/search?q=cache:PYvkJOk0afIJ:https://www.forbes.com/sites/chloesorvino/2015/01/27/successful-african-american-real-estate-mogul-inches-closer-to-billionaire-status/+&cd=4&hl=en&ct=clnk&gl=us). Decades earlier, Peebles dropped out of Rutgers after his freshman year to get his real estate license.

"I was kind of bored with school," Peebles [told](https://csq.com/2020/06/how-don-peebles-became-one-of-the-wealthiest-african-american-real-estate-developers-in-the-united-states/#.YEeJhmhKiUk) C-Suite Quarterly. "I wanted to be busier."

## H. Wayne Huizenga

![Image 29: Man with Armload of Videos ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/3b7b5992-2717-4e37-95af-c26a6553750b/thumbnail/620x372/f775a3300a177c1080de457dccaa02e5/dropouts-huizenga.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

Obituaries of [H. Wayne Huizenga](https://www.gainesville.com/news/20180323/wayne-huizenga-who-went-from-trash-to-billions-dies-at-80) in 2018 led with the tidbit that the man who built Blockbuster into a brand name, and owned three pro sports franchises, including the NFL's Miami Dolphins, was a once-upon-a-time dropout of Michigan's Calvin College.

## Rachel Lim

![Image 30: dropouts-lim.jpg ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/512ee79f-bcdd-41c9-b079-50b5390e8474/thumbnail/620x363/094f02e1f180cab485a290248a2bac1c/dropouts-lim.jpg#)

 TedX Talks via YouTube/screenshot 

Rachel Lim is a co-founder of Love, Bonito, [described](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/05/advice-on-starting-a-business-after-dropping-out-of-college-university.html) by CNBC as a"multimillion-dollar" fashion brand.

Lim was months away from graduating from Nanyang Technological University in her native Singapore when she bet on her then-fledgling business.

"I was juggling school and work, and I wasn't excelling in both, and I realized that I had to focus on one," Lim [told](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/03/love-bonito-ceo-rachel-lim-built-a-multimillion-dollar-fashion-empire.html) CNBC.

## Harry Truman

![Image 31: Harry S. Truman In Floral Armchair ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/6b0320d6-c6cd-43c8-81c0-f5ccdc4615f7/thumbnail/620x372/8c1ee2bb03b61d72c9bbd79c216a2b22/dropouts-truman.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

Harry Truman is the second college dropout to serve as U.S. president in the 20th century.

Sources generally list Truman's higher-education resume as consisting of a semester at an unnamed Kansas City, Missouri, business school, and night classes at what was then known as [Kansas City Law School](https://www.upi.com/Archives/1945/04/12/Truman-becomes-32nd-president/2181428401436/). He didn't earn a degree at either campus.

## Paul Allen

![Image 32: Arizona Cardinals v Seattle Seahawks ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/1bbc4594-5311-4708-bc57-f57c629ed2ea/thumbnail/620x372/f0b97ecbd1312430873f8d2bc401306e/dropouts-allen.jpg#)

 Steve Dykes/Getty Images 

The late Paul Allen is another college dropout who went on to become a billionaire NFL owner. Allen [left Washington State University](https://magazine.washington.edu/feature/paul-allen-living-computers/) after two years to take a job in Boston — where, not coincidentally, his high school computer pal Bill Gates had enrolled at Harvard. A co-founder of Microsoft, Allen owned the Seattle Seahawks from 1997 until his death in 2018.

## Paula Abdul

![Image 33: Paula Abdul Portrait ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/ef54ed0b-da2c-4338-a235-aacc585d054c/thumbnail/620x386/b661e9af04bcf9e94c6054f8b2c40b68/dropouts-abdul.jpg#)

 Michel Linssen/Redferns/Getty Images 

According to Cal State Northridge, future Grammy winner and TV host Paula Abdul [studied broadcast journalism and participated in cheer](https://www.csun.edu/magazine/homepage/matadors-mic) at the suburban Los Angeles campus from 1980-1984. Hired as a Los Angeles Lakers cheerleader [as a freshman](https://www.csun.edu/node/161961), Adbul left school, sans a degree, as her dance and choreography career heated up.

## Frank Lloyd Wright

![Image 34: Frank Lloyd Wright ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/d48def34-95de-4753-b571-c27060dc6ad0/thumbnail/620x372/52b71c3ae5e391094ef525eef963f4f4/dropouts-wright.jpg#)

 Peter Stackpole/The LIFE Picture Collection via Getty Images 

According to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Frank Lloyd Wright "[took classes part-time for two semesters](https://ls.wisc.edu/news/busted-frank-lloyd-wright-failed-to-appear-in-class/)" there in the late 1880s. That was the beginning and end of Wright's college career. He would go on to design New York City's Guggenheim Museum, and be hailed in his lifetime as "[the greatest architect of the 20th Century](http://content.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1704183_1704185_1704243,00.html)."

## Ty Warner

![Image 35: H. Ty Warner ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7e4c351e-ca37-4361-b67e-726b05850324/thumbnail/620x372/2ef7f52efb07e91581fae74239c06f3f/dropouts-warner.jpg#)

 Kevin Horan/The LIFE Images Collection/Getty Images 

Life hasn't always been smooth for the billionaire mogul behind Beanie Babies. In [court documents](https://www.scribd.com/document/195307593/Ty-Warner-filing-ahead-of-sentencing-on-tax-evasion-conviction#fullscreen&from_embed), it was stated that Ty Warner had to drop out of Michigan's Kalamazoo College in the early 1960s "because he could no longer afford tuition." Warner [pleaded guilty](https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2013/09/18/beanie-baby-founder-to-plead-guilty-to-tax-evasion/) to tax evasion in 2013.

## Jamaica Kincaid

![Image 36: Festival Delle Letterature Di Roma 2010 ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/c19ed2b2-a1c2-4002-9595-07da2a4086a4/thumbnail/620x372/85db34b6e58047f51b8cd95f5cd2640f/dropouts-kincaid.jpg#)

 Elisabetta A. Villa/Getty Images 

On her way to becoming an acclaimed author, Jamaica Kincaid took night classes in photography at the New School for Social Research in New York City. She would go on to attend New Hampshire's Franconia College, she would [say](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2931581?seq=1), "because I thought maybe I should go to college." But writing assignments beckoned — and Kincaid left school to nab them.

## Steve Madden

![Image 37: Shoe Designer Steve Madden ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/bdaafe9e-57d8-4ba0-b857-2d645796a7a1/thumbnail/620x380/417e7113cf3ac0fe71c6eb8f5d72fe98/dropouts-madden.jpg#)

 Tom Herde/The Boston Globe via Getty Images 

"I didn't last long there," footwear designer and fashion mogul [Steve Madden](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/steve-madden-on-putting-his-best-foot-forward/) once [told](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/steve-madden-on-putting-his-best-foot-forward/) CBS News of his college years at the University of Miami.

Madden dropped out after his father stopped paying the tuition and ordered the disinterested student to get a job.

## Sean "Diddy" Combs

![Image 38: Sean "Diddy" Combs Delivers Commencement Address at Howard University ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/8963c6d1-f2e3-4066-a589-c440300112d5/thumbnail/620x372/baeb653e2b8aafb5d351089b8335c045/dropouts-combs.jpg#)

 Allison Shelley/Getty Images 

In 2014, [Sean "Diddy" Combs](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/sean-combs/2/) was a commencement speaker at Howard University. The future Bad Boy music mogul and Sean John fashion entrepreneur[dropped out of the school](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/reliable-source/wp/2014/04/15/sean-combs-howard-dropout-to-give-commencement-speech/)in 1990 after two years of study.

## Ryan Seacrest

![Image 39: 60th Annual GRAMMY Awards - Arrivals ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/c782ac0f-a14e-4693-ad63-78c83a01c21c/thumbnail/620x372/dbce4cd26ed6dcbb6d84fa4dcc4ff982/dropouts-seacrest.jpg#)

 Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic/Getty Images 

Ryan Seacrest studied journalism for one year at the University of Georgia before [dropping out](https://www.redandblack.com/uganews/12-notable-former-uga-students-who-never-graduated-from-the-university/article_68d97b66-1804-11e6-8e0e-3be1deb32f74.html) in 1992, according to the campus news outlet, the Red & Black. ## Lady Gaga

![Image 40: The 2019 Met Gala Celebrating Camp: Notes On Fashion - Arrivals ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/41126986-ed09-4e5f-9d22-b68203f01f48/thumbnail/620x372/49a35cd504b205c42e4a61c05519d881/dropouts-gaga.jpg#)

 Karwai Tang/Getty Images 

New York University's Tisch Drama includes the Grammy- and Oscar-winning [Lady Gaga](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lady-gaga-chromatica/) on [its alumni list](https://tisch.nyu.edu/drama/alumni/alumnilist); the former Stefani Germanotta attended the school in the late 2000s, but did not stick around to graduate.

## James Dean

![Image 41: On the set of Rebel Without a Cause ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/1a140598-1031-4083-95a1-11cc95086d0f/thumbnail/620x361/295c0ded6e3004a22ed448b7368545c6/dropouts-dean.jpg#)

 Sunset Boulevard/Corbis via Getty Images 

James Dean [arrived at UCLA](https://optimism.ucla.edu/profiles/dean/) in 1950 as a pre-law transfer student from Santa Monica College. In short order, the future "Rebel Without a Cause" icon changed his major to drama, won his first stage role in a campus production of "Macbeth," [got a bad review](https://webcache.googleusercontent.com/search?q=cache:xFodXDca7TcJ:https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1991-04-09-9102010611-story.html+&cd=2&hl=en&ct=clnk&gl=us) — and dropped out to try his luck on the New York stage.

## Paul Newman

![Image 42: Paul Newman ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7963117a-10d1-4db2-915d-54957e74fdf2/thumbnail/620x378/7c61084b54df3629725ecd626c36eb2e/dropouts-newman.jpg#)

 Art Zelin/Getty Images 

Like James Dean a year before him, Paul Newman dropped out of college — in Newman's case, [Yale](https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2008/09/29/paul-newman-legend-from-yale-drama-dies-at-83/) — to head to New York. Newman and Dean would both become famous for their movies and for helping popularize the methods of method acting.

## Bonnie Raitt

![Image 43: 62nd Annual GRAMMY Awards – Arrivals ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/f9760f01-ef2c-41e3-b454-a455b0effe26/thumbnail/620x375/a4628523dc06264761a16e12d47fbd79/dropouts-raitt.jpg#)

 Frazer Harrison/Getty Images for The Recording Academy 

The daughter of Broadway star John Raitt, Bonnie Raitt was an African studies major at Harvard's Radcliffe College when she fell in with the blues music scene that would take her to Philadelphia (her first break from college) and a 1970 tour with the Rolling Stones (her second break).

## Travis Kalanick

![Image 44: Key Speakers At The Institute of Directors Annual Convention ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7dfcf466-c2ba-4776-966d-5c5397c4c6b7/thumbnail/620x372/6da65f622c8a1764788f0145d3f6bbcb/dropouts-kalanick.jpg#)

 Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

When [Travis Kalanick](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/uber-co-founder-former-ceo-travis-kalanick-to-leave-board-after-selling-2-5-billion-in-company-shares/) dropped out of UCLA, his disappointed parents held their tongue because, as his dad once [explained to the HuffPost](https://www.huffpost.com/entry/uber-travis-kalanick-talk-to-me_n_57040082e4b0daf53af126a9#:~:text=As%20part%20of%20HuffPost's%20new,finding%20happiness%20later%20in%20life.), they "knew something was going to work out for [him]." And it did. In 2009, Kalanick co-founded the ride-hailing giant Uber.

## Michael Dell

![Image 45: Michael Dell, chairman of Dell Inc., speaks at a news confer ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7d4539a4-0dcb-4ba0-abd6-3e2db7ffb29b/thumbnail/620x372/65794263370d98d74411dca51ceb229a/dropouts-dell.jpg#)

 Bloomberg/Getty Images 

"If you don't know, I should confess," tech mogul Michael Dell [said in an address](https://news.utexas.edu/2019/05/26/michael-dell-urges-graduates-not-just-to-succeed-but-to-serve/) at the University of Texas at Austin's 2019 spring commencement. ## Eddie Murphy

![Image 46: Critics' Choice Association The Celebration Of Black Cinema ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/4063f179-7789-4861-a9a7-982f32c56e4a/thumbnail/620x372/6a4d015a85aff0354560bf0facc577a9/dropouts-murphy.jpg#)

 Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Niche Imports 

According to an early Newsday [profile of the comic actor](https://www.newsday.com/long-island/archive-roosevelt-s-eddie-murphy-laughs-his-way-to-the-top-1.11398854) in 1981, Eddie Murphy attended New York's Nassau Community College for two weeks. Not long after, he would drop into "Saturday Night Live," and, at age 19, become a breakout star.

## R. Buckminster Fuller

![Image 47: Buckminster Fuller in Front of Dome ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/b5c57129-e237-4cdc-b729-90926fb6852f/thumbnail/620x372/65d907b27ed66ab2a158e7af43c17189/dropouts-fuller.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

R. Buckminster Fuller, the innovative architect and engineer who gave the world the geodesic dome, is a two-time college dropout via expulsion. In 1914, per Fuller's official biography by the Buckminster Fuller Institute, the future great was dismissed from Harvard "[after excessively socializing and missing his midterm exams](https://www.bfi.org/about-fuller/biography)." Upon a return to campus in 1915, Fuller was expelled again.

## Ted Turner

![Image 48: Portrait of Ted Turner ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/646c509c-4834-4ef5-acd0-5e9368ba5161/thumbnail/620x372/8958b8347ad1af0f93ecee7dd20a7571/dropouts-turner.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

CNN founder and former Atlanta Braves MLB owner Ted Turner is another who left college via expulsion. According to a New Yorker profile, Turner was kicked out of Brown University "[for smuggling a coed into his room](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2001/04/23/the-lost-tycoon)." Within a few years, Turner's father would commit suicide and the 24-year-old would inherit and exponentially grow the family's advertising company.

## Johnny Chan

![Image 49: NBC's 4th National Heads-Up Poker Championship ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/07e233b3-3428-4ad3-abce-846b6660983f/thumbnail/620x372/73b25cd46947984b504d42bd2fafd846/dropouts-chan.jpg#)

 Ethan Miller/Getty Images 

In the 1970s, future professional poker champ Johnny Chan studied hotel and restaurant management at the University of Houston. But he dropped out at age 21.

"I just couldn't work 9 to 5," Chan [told](https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/news/911-dispatch-worker-coronavirus-covid-shift-collapsed-investigation-11535714) New Times. "The action always gets me. The action makes me who I am."

## Dustin Moskovitz

![Image 50: Keynote Speakers At TechCrunch Disrupt Conference ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/0a26f656-7503-46b8-99f4-48b2e4745cf6/thumbnail/620x372/d71fc33f5c312ea15c3c124a6ad87d3e/dropouts-moskovitz.jpg#)

 Noah Berger/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

Dustin Moskovitz dropped out of Harvard along with roommate Mark Zuckerberg to work on Facebook. The co-founder of the social media giant [told](https://www.startups.com/library/founder-stories/dustin-moskovitz) Startups.com that it wasn't their intent to "permanently" leave the campus.

![Image 51: 25th Anniversary Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony - Press Room ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/4c6145ce-696e-4419-92fd-1b9291dad191/thumbnail/620x370/beba3cf85fec742df33b902c2cb5b01f/dropouts-geffen.jpg#)

 Stephen Lovekin/Getty Images 

David Geffen dropped out of the University of Texas at Austin after less than a year, according to a [PBS timeline](https://www.pbs.org/wnet/americanmasters/david-geffen-timeline-year-by-year-how-david-geffen-invented-himself/2358/) of the agent turned media mogul. ![Image 52: Steve Wozniak with an Apple IIe ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/388a986f-e14f-4d50-a501-9112ab429768/thumbnail/620x372/8dfcba97e43aac77b39ac52e339e3736/dropouts-woz.jpg#)

# 50 super successful college dropouts

 By Joal Ryan

March 18, 2021 / 3:15 PM EDT / CBS News

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

![Image 4: 2018 MoMA David Rockefeller Award Luncheon Honoring Oprah Winfrey ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/8f488567-13ec-4afa-ba12-e5b8d2c446ce/thumbnail/620x372/74847a6a9f75bd90fa3e4de4193d8f6a/dropouts-oprah.jpg#)

 Gonzalo Marroquin/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images 

For many, college provides a road to success. But it's not the only road. Here's a look at dozens of tech, business, political and media stars of the 20th century and beyond who left school without undergrad degrees, but with plenty of ambition and talent to make things happen.

First up: [Oprah Winfrey](https://www.cbsnews.com/video/oprah-winfrey-on-her-bombshell-harry-and-meghan-interview/).

In 1975, the future media mogul and philanthropist left Tennessee State University for a TV job one credit shy of completing her four-year degree. A decade later, after launching her talk show and earning an Oscar nomination, Winfrey resumed her studies. She graduated as a member of Tennessee State's Class of 1986.

## Steve Jobs

![Image 5: T-Mobile Gets iPhone Germany Contract ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/d9a05f7f-cd28-4588-9f32-2a5df65155c8/thumbnail/620x372/6014e3fdc8aefaa43706effd7af3b43e/dropouts-jobs.jpg#)

 Sean Gallup/Getty Images 

The Apple co-founder "may ... be one of the most famous dropouts in history," per [Reed College](https://www.reed.edu/steve-jobs.html#:~:text=As%20everyone%20knows%2C%20Steve%20Jobs,%2C%20but%20didn't%20graduate.&text=Questioning%20everything%20and%20everyone%2C%20Steve,designing%20the%20revolutionary%20Apple%20Macintosh.), the liberal arts school in Oregon which [Steve Jobs](https://www.cbsnews.com/feature/steve-jobs-1955-2011/) left after just one semester. ("I ran out of money," Jobs [explained](https://www.reed.edu/reed-magazine/articles/2018/steve-jobs-staying-hungry.html) in a 1991 commencement speech at the school.)

## Mark Zuckerberg

![Image 6: Facebook Founder Mark Zuckerberg Delivers Commencement Address At Harvard ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/e70f1918-e28a-42a1-a1e3-2a08b4ce0a7e/thumbnail/620x372/7426fdf0fa500c905836f358ba5bea81/dropouts-zuckerberg.jpg#)

 Paul Marotta/Getty Images 

In 2017, the Facebook CEO was a commencement speaker at Harvard University. [Mark Zuckerberg](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/facebook-ceo-mark-zuckerberg-wife-priscilla-chan-inside-their-home-family-life/) dropped out of the Ivy League school in 2005 to focus on his then-young but growing social media platform.

## Alicia Keys

![Image 7: 62nd Annual GRAMMY Awards - Show ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/3567dcfd-c05e-415e-8c57-31d498dd126d/thumbnail/620x372/7ad0bdc8597a9528429bcbb30da80e5f/dropouts-keys.jpg#)

 Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic/Getty Images 

In the late 1990s, according to an Oprah magazine [interview with singer-songwriter Alicia Keys](https://www.oprah.com/omagazine/oprahs-interview-with-alicia-keys), the future Grammy-winner left Columbia University after four weeks for a music deal with Columbia Records. She was all of 16 at the time.

## Dick Cheney

![Image 8: Dick Cheney Made a Statement ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/dc64545d-2401-4469-8271-f7054d1ea320/thumbnail/620x372/d377823c38201aa00c0ce3cc2426ea2f/dropouts-cheney.jpg#)

 Alex Wong/Newsmakers/Getty Images 

According to the [Yale Daily News](https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2003/09/19/famous-failures/), [Dick Cheney](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/never-before-seen-photos-of-bush-administration-during-9-11/11/) dropped out of the Ivy League school _twice_. (Biography.com and other sources describe the departures as Cheney having "[failed out](https://www.biography.com/news/dick-cheney-political-rise-vice-president).")

The future U.S. vice president would eventually settle into higher education and earn bachelor's and master's degrees at the University of Wyoming.

## Joel Osteen

![Image 9: Today - Season 62 ](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/2ad58c54-ff60-44eb-aef5-7e0266dd06e4/thumbnail/620x372/6ad048405b81bfa0910ab9fab133b586/dropouts-osteen.jpg#)

 Peter Kramer/NBC/NBC Newswire/NBCUniversal/Getty Images 

[Joel Osteen](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/the-positivity-of-joel-osteen/)dropped out of Oral Roberts University as a freshman in the early 1980s. The pastor went on to help build his father's Houston evangelical church, Lakewood, into the [biggest megachurch in the United States](https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/30-biggest-american-megachurches-ranked/30/), with about 43,500 weekly visitors in pre-COVID times.

## Tiger Woods

![Image 10: California v Stanford ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/68c3d28d-702e-4d31-97c8-a079d320da16/thumbnail/620x372/5b38f929e04d5306422adda6d426bd69/dropouts-woods.jpg#)

 Ezra Shaw/Getty Images 

Like many elite athletes, Tiger Woods left college early to pursue his sport professionally. In his case, he exited Stanford after his sophomore year. "[T]he only regret I have in life is not spending another year at Stanford," Woods [said](https://golf.com/news/tiger-woods-reveals-his-greatest-regret-to-charlie-rose/) in 2016.

## Bill Gates

![Image 11: Microsoft Co-founder Bill Gates ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/daf667f2-5b97-4631-9934-670467ca2f7f/thumbnail/620x372/895fed25400967c490e84acb4d2c932f/dropouts-gates.jpg#)

 Doug Wilson/CORBIS/Corbis/Getty Images 

The future philanthropist [left Harvard](https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2013/09/dawn-of-a-revolution/) after the end of his sophomore year. He would return, but drop out for good after completing his junior year. Both times, [Bill Gates](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bill-gates-climate-change-disaster-60-minutes-2021-02-14/) exited school to focus on the company he co-founded in 1975: Microsoft.

## Brad Pitt

![Image 12: 86th Annual Academy Awards - Arrivals ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/32f40097-a774-4fb5-87f4-7fb321c726b8/thumbnail/620x372/c2c0e6addb0dd911d95e54fc8b9df16e/dropouts-pitt.jpg#)

When [Travis Kalanick](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/uber-co-founder-former-ceo-travis-kalanick-to-leave-board-after-selling-2-5-billion-in-company-shares/) dropped out of UCLA, his disappointed parents held their tongue because, as his dad once [explained to the HuffPost](https://www.huffpost.com/entry/uber-travis-kalanick-talk-to-me_n_57040082e4b0daf53af126a9#:~:text=As%20part%20of%20HuffPost's%20new,finding%20happiness%20later%20in%20life.), they "knew something was going to work out for [him]." And it did. In 2009, Kalanick co-founded the ride-hailing giant Uber.

## Michael Dell

![Image 45: Michael Dell, chairman of Dell Inc., speaks at a news confer ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/7d4539a4-0dcb-4ba0-abd6-3e2db7ffb29b/thumbnail/620x372/65794263370d98d74411dca51ceb229a/dropouts-dell.jpg#)

 Bloomberg/Getty Images 

"If you don't know, I should confess," tech mogul Michael Dell [said in an address](https://news.utexas.edu/2019/05/26/michael-dell-urges-graduates-not-just-to-succeed-but-to-serve/) at the University of Texas at Austin's 2019 spring commencement. "I dropped out of UT after two semesters." Dell was in a hurry to devote himself to his namesake computing business.

## Eddie Murphy

![Image 46: Critics' Choice Association The Celebration Of Black Cinema ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/4063f179-7789-4861-a9a7-982f32c56e4a/thumbnail/620x372/6a4d015a85aff0354560bf0facc577a9/dropouts-murphy.jpg#)

 Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Niche Imports 

According to an early Newsday [profile of the comic actor](https://www.newsday.com/long-island/archive-roosevelt-s-eddie-murphy-laughs-his-way-to-the-top-1.11398854) in 1981, Eddie Murphy attended New York's Nassau Community College for two weeks. Not long after, he would drop into "Saturday Night Live," and, at age 19, become a breakout star.

## R. Buckminster Fuller

![Image 47: Buckminster Fuller in Front of Dome ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/b5c57129-e237-4cdc-b729-90926fb6852f/thumbnail/620x372/65d907b27ed66ab2a158e7af43c17189/dropouts-fuller.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

R. Buckminster Fuller, the innovative architect and engineer who gave the world the geodesic dome, is a two-time college dropout via expulsion. In 1914, per Fuller's official biography by the Buckminster Fuller Institute, the future great was dismissed from Harvard "[after excessively socializing and missing his midterm exams](https://www.bfi.org/about-fuller/biography)." Upon a return to campus in 1915, Fuller was expelled again.

## Ted Turner

![Image 48: Portrait of Ted Turner ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/646c509c-4834-4ef5-acd0-5e9368ba5161/thumbnail/620x372/8958b8347ad1af0f93ecee7dd20a7571/dropouts-turner.jpg#)

 Bettmann/Getty Images 

CNN founder and former Atlanta Braves MLB owner Ted Turner is another who left college via expulsion. According to a New Yorker profile, Turner was kicked out of Brown University "[for smuggling a coed into his room](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2001/04/23/the-lost-tycoon)." Within a few years, Turner's father would commit suicide and the 24-year-old would inherit and exponentially grow the family's advertising company.

## Johnny Chan

![Image 49: NBC's 4th National Heads-Up Poker Championship ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/07e233b3-3428-4ad3-abce-846b6660983f/thumbnail/620x372/73b25cd46947984b504d42bd2fafd846/dropouts-chan.jpg#)

 Ethan Miller/Getty Images 

In the 1970s, future professional poker champ Johnny Chan studied hotel and restaurant management at the University of Houston. But he dropped out at age 21.

"I just couldn't work 9 to 5," Chan [told](https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/news/911-dispatch-worker-coronavirus-covid-shift-collapsed-investigation-11535714) New Times. "The action always gets me. The action makes me who I am."

## Dustin Moskovitz

![Image 50: Keynote Speakers At TechCrunch Disrupt Conference ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/0a26f656-7503-46b8-99f4-48b2e4745cf6/thumbnail/620x372/d71fc33f5c312ea15c3c124a6ad87d3e/dropouts-moskovitz.jpg#)

 Noah Berger/Bloomberg/Getty Images 

Dustin Moskovitz dropped out of Harvard along with roommate Mark Zuckerberg to work on Facebook. The co-founder of the social media giant [told](https://www.startups.com/library/founder-stories/dustin-moskovitz) Startups.com that it wasn't their intent to "permanently" leave the campus.

"[But] it would be impossible to run the company while we were also going to school," Moskovitz said. "I don't know how we thought that was ever going to work."

## David Geffen

![Image 51: 25th Anniversary Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony - Press Room ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/4c6145ce-696e-4419-92fd-1b9291dad191/thumbnail/620x370/beba3cf85fec742df33b902c2cb5b01f/dropouts-geffen.jpg#)

 Stephen Lovekin/Getty Images 

David Geffen dropped out of the University of Texas at Austin after less than a year, according to a [PBS timeline](https://www.pbs.org/wnet/americanmasters/david-geffen-timeline-year-by-year-how-david-geffen-invented-himself/2358/) of the agent turned media mogul. Geffen went on to co-found DreamWorks with Jeffrey Katzenberg and fellow college dropout Steven Spielberg.

## Steve Wozniak

![Image 52: Steve Wozniak with an Apple IIe ](https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/388a986f-e14f-4d50-a501-9112ab429768/thumbnail/620x372/8dfcba97e43aac77b39ac52e339e3736/dropouts-woz.jpg#)

 Roger Ressmeyer/CORBIS/VCG/Getty Images 

According to Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, he "[never dropped out](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-05-14-vw-5389-story.html)" out of the University of California, Berkeley — he "simply took a year off to earn money for [his] fourth year of school," and didn't return for more than a decade.

True to his word, if not timeline, Wozniak [earned his bachelor's of science degree](https://engineering.berkeley.edu/steve-wozniak-inventor-and-apple-co-founder/) from Berkeley in 1986.

## Micky Arison

![Image 53: Heat Practice for Game 3 of NBA Finals ](https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2021/03/09/d91c510a-83f3-4f56-810c-bc0a6f4bc459/thumbnail/620x372/c3908e32dd3f323a4bb51ca6a9f3e8fe/dropouts-arison.jpg#)

 David Santiago/El Nuevo Herald/Tribune News Service/Getty Images 

Micky Arison dropped out of the University of Miami to help his father, Ted Arison, run the one-ship operation that originally was Carnival Cruise Lines. He would become a regular on [lists of the world's wealthiest people](https://www.sportscasting.com/is-the-miami-heats-micky-arison-the-richest-owner-in-the-nba/), and hoist three NBA Finals trophies as owner of the Miami Heat.

One late summer afternoon in San Francisco, some 200 people in their early 20s arrived at the Marina Theater, an old-style movie theater with musty felt seats. The group, almost entirely male, came from all over: India, New Zealand, Ohio, New York. They wore chintzy black robes bought on Amazon, sweatshirts emblazoned with hackathon logos and, occasionally, Rolexes.

They had gathered for a “Dropout Graduation” in San Francisco, a tongue-in-cheek commencement ceremony for students who chose to never have one. Unsurprisingly, it had [been organized](https://x.com/ali_debow/status/1903976274046930979) on X.

* * *

Read

[The Good Life, According to Gen Z](https://www.thefp.com/p/why-my-generation-is-giving-up-on)

* * *

It used to be that college dropout success stories were the rarest of exceptions. Steve Jobs, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, Jack Dorsey—all were the superhuman oddballs who left Harvard and Stanford and were the better for it, going on to build billion-dollar empires while defining themselves against the traditional path college offered.

For everyone else, college was a rite of passage. A degree meant status, employability, and upward mobility.

Over the past decade, that promise has eroded.

One late summer afternoon in San Francisco, some 200 people in their early 20s arrived at the Marina Theater, an old-style movie theater with musty felt seats. The group, almost entirely male, came from all over: India, New Zealand, Ohio, New York. They wore chintzy black robes bought on Amazon, sweatshirts emblazoned with hackathon logos and, occasionally, Rolexes.

They had gathered for a “Dropout Graduation” in San Francisco, a tongue-in-cheek commencement ceremony for students who chose to never have one. Unsurprisingly, it had [been organized](https://x.com/ali_debow/status/1903976274046930979) on X.

It used to be that college dropout success stories were the rarest of exceptions. Steve Jobs, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, Jack Dorsey—all were the superhuman oddballs who left Harvard and Stanford and were the better for it, going on to build billion-dollar empires while defining themselves against the traditional path college offered.

For everyone else, college was a rite of passage. A degree meant status, employability, and upward mobility.

Over the past decade, that promise has eroded.

# About The Free Press

The Free Press is a [new media company](https://www.thefp.com/p/welcome-to-the-free-press) founded by Bari Weiss and built on the ideals that once were the bedrock of great American journalism: honesty, doggedness, and fierce independence. We publish investigative stories and provocative commentary about the world as it actually is—with the quality once expected from the legacy press, but the fearlessness of the new.

Originally called _Common Sense_, we focus on stories that are ignored or misconstrued in the service of an ideological narrative. For us, curiosity isn’t a liability. It’s a necessity.

Expect debates, scoops from trusted reporters, provocations from those thinking outside the lines, and live events that bring people with different views together into a truly diverse community.

You won’t agree with everything we run. And we think that’s exactly the point.

# Our Values

At _The Free Press_, we hold ourselves to a consistent set of values that guide our coverage, our behavior, and our treatment of others. From our leadership, to our employees, to our investors, we co-sign the following:

_**Honesty**_

We seek and report the truth. We tell it plainly when we uncover it, even when it’s politically inconvenient.

_**Curiosity**_

For others, curiosity has become a liability. At _The Free Press_, we believe an open mind is fundamental to doing good journalism.

_**Respect**_

We assume good faith. We treat each other and our sources with the utmost respect.

_**Hard Work**_

Great journalism takes hard work, and we embrace it. We require the old-fashioned reporter skill set—empathy, courage, ingenuity, and drive—for everyone on our team.

_**Independence**_

We are proudly not a political monolith. Independence isn’t just a journalistic value for us; it’s also fundamental to the way we are building our business.

_**Excellence**_

We take tremendous pride in being best-in-class. We have faith that success will follow if we relentlessly focus on delivering an excellent product every day to our audience.

_**Common****Sense**_

We are adults, and we treat our readers like adults, too. We encourage each other to think for ourselves and change our minds when we encounter new information.

_**Belief in the American Project**_

Our reporting and opinion can be harshly critical of our country and its leaders, but that is because we believe deeply in America and its promise. We make no apology for making distinctions between good and bad, liberalism and illiberalism, the rule of the law and mob rule, freedom and unfreedom—and we advocate forcefully for the former.

The debate around whether college is worth the [time and money](https://www.businessinsider.com/is-college-still-worth-it-tech-execs-kids-2026-5) has been heating up.

As AI reshapes what it means to be a white-collar worker, and amid [high tuition fees](https://www.businessinsider.com/most-expensive-colleges-tuition-in-us), some young people are rethinking the traditional path of [graduating from college](https://www.businessinsider.com/colleges-highest-earning-graduates-every-state) before entering the workforce.

By now, stories of [Mark Zuckerberg](https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg) and Bill Gates dropping out of college before earning their degrees have become tech-industry folklore. However, the Meta and Microsoft founders aren't the only influential executives who have risen to the top without finishing college.

The founders and CEOs of other tech companies — including [a new generation](https://www.businessinsider.com/gen-z-tech-founders-skipping-college-new-dropping-out-palantir-2025-6) of Gen Z AI talent — also left higher education to bet on the tech world.

Here are 21 tech executives who never got their college degrees.

## Mark Zuckerberg — founder and CEO, Meta

![Image 2: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Zuckerberg is pictured wearing the Ray-Ban Meta glasses.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Zuckerberg, founder and [CEO of Meta](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-launches-muse-spark-1-1-cost-effective-ai-2026-7), studied psychology and computer science at Harvard but left without completing a degree.

In 2004, while a student at Harvard University, he launched "thefacebook.com," which later became Facebook, but he dropped out during his sophomore year to move to Palo Alto and work on his company full-time.

"It's sort of been this taboo thing to say, maybe not everyone needs to go to college because there's, like, a lot of jobs that don't require that," [Zuckerberg told comedian Theo Von](https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg-theo-von-harvard-interview-2025-4) in a 2025 interview. "But I think people are probably coming around to that opinion a little more now than maybe like 10 years ago."

Zuckerberg received an honorary degree from Harvard in 2017.

## Sam Altman — cofounder and CEO, OpenAI

![Image 4: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Sam Altman said in an interview in 2025 that he's "envious" of the new generation of college dropouts.Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images

[Sam Altman studied computer science](https://www.businessinsider.com/sam-altman-openai-envies-college-dropouts-stanford-devday-2025-10) at Stanford University for two years before dropping out in 2005 at the age of 19.

He left to cofound location-sharing app Loopt, which was acquired in 2012 by Green Dot.

Altman became president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator in 2014. He [cofounded OpenAI](https://www.businessinsider.com/sam-altman) in 2015, alongside Elon Musk and other founders, and he became the CEO in 2019.

Altman said in an interview at the DevDay conference in 2025 that he is "envious of the current generation of 20-year-old dropouts."

"The amount of stuff you can build, the opportunity in this space is so incredibly wide," he said.

## John and Patrick Collison — cofounders, Stripe

![Image 6: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

John Collison (left) is the cofounder and president of Stripe, while his cofounder brother, Patrick Collison (right), is the CEO.Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Win McNamee/Getty Images

John and Patrick Collison grew up in Ireland. As teenagers, they hatched the idea for their first business, an online auction management company named Auctomatic.

The brothers sold Auctomatic in 2008 for $5 million, making them teen millionaires, [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2008/mar/27/technology.news) reported.

[Patrick Collison](https://www.businessinsider.com/the-stripe-ceo-floats-creating-software-on-demand-sell-off-2026-3) enrolled at MIT in 2006, but dropped out to work on his business ventures, while John Collison started at Harvard in 2009 and dropped out a year later to work on their new payments company, Stripe.

The brothers launched Stripe in 2010. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/24/stripe-value-stock-sale-tender-offer.html) reported that it was valued at $159 billion earlier this year.

## Mustafa Suleyman — CEO, Microsoft AI

![Image 8: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI.Stephen Brashear/Getty Images

Mustafa Suleyman grew up in London and studied philosophy and theology at Oxford University. He dropped out as the degree felt ["abstract and impractical"](https://www.businessinsider.com/mustafa-suleyman-the-lefty-activist-ensuring-google-deepmind-benefits-all-of-humanity-2017-12) to him.

After leaving university, Suleyman set up the Muslim Youth Helpline, a telephone counseling service, with a friend from university.

After working for several years in politics and consulting, Suleyman cofounded DeepMind in 2010.

In 2024, Suleyman became the executive vice president and CEO of the newly founded Microsoft AI.

## Melanie Perkins — cofounder and CEO, Canva

![Image 10: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Melanie Perkins is the cofounder and CEO of Canva.Nina Franova/Getty Images for SXSW Sydney

Melanie Perkins grew up in Perth, Australia, and attended the University of Western Australia, where she came up with the [idea of making design](https://apac.entrepreneur.com/women-entrepreneur/how-this-30-year-old-college-dropout-created-a-tech-unicorn/329883) easier, she told Entrepreneur in 2019.

Perkins launched [Fusion Books](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-42552367), a website that enables students to design their own yearbooks, with her then-boyfriend (and now-husband), Clifford Obrecht, in 2007.

She told the [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/business-42552367) that she decided to drop out of college, believing the concept could be applied to projects beyond yearbooks. Perkins began meeting investors in Silicon Valley in 2010.

In 2013, Perkins and Obrecht launched Canva. The company was valued at $42 billion in a 2025 employee share sale.

## Daniel Ek — cofounder and executive chair, Spotify

![Image 12: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Daniel Ek transitioned to the role of executive chair from CEO at the beginning of 2026.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Daniel Ek grew up in Sweden and enrolled at the country's KTH Royal Institute of Technology in 2002 to study engineering.

In an interview with [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevenbertoni/2012/01/04/spotifys-daniel-ek-the-most-important-man-in-music/#7cf824c664ca) in 2012, he said he lasted only eight weeks, when he found out his entire first year would be devoted to theoretical mathematics. He soon started taking gigs at various tech companies.

Ek cofounded Spotify in 2006, where he was the CEO until 2025. CNBC reported that he became a billionaire in 2018 when Spotify listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

## Larry Ellison — cofounder and CTO, Oracle

![Image 14: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Oracle cofounder Larry Ellison.[Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/oracle-co-founder-cto-and-executive-chairman-larry-ellison-news-photo/2197466221)

As a kid growing up in Chicago, [Larry Ellison](https://www.businessinsider.com/larry-ellison-shares-what-dropping-out-of-college-and-getting-divorced-taught-him-about-success-2016-5) planned to attend medical school at USC, get married and have kids, and move to Los Angeles to work as a doctor.

However, that never happened. [He tried to earn an undergraduate degree](https://www.businessinsider.com/rise-of-oracle-founder-larry-ellison-2017-1)twice: once at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (for two years) and again at the University of Chicago (where he lasted one semester).

After dropping out a second time, Ellison moved to California amid the burgeoning tech scene, where he cofounded what later became Oracle in 1977.

He now serves as the company's chief technology officer and, as of 2026, Forbes reported he remains one of the richest people in the world.

## Alexandr Wang — founder and former CEO, Scale AI; chief AI officer, Meta

![Image 16: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Alexandr Wang was named the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2021.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Born in Los Alamos, New Mexico, [Alexandr Wang](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-ai-model-catches-up-openai-gpt-5-says-2026-7) studied mathematics and computer science at MIT, according to his LinkedIn profile, before dropping out at 19 to launch Scale AI.

Forbes reported that Wang became the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2021, when he was 24. He held the title until he was overtaken by Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan in 2025.

He was the CEO of Scale AI until 2025, when [Meta spent roughly $14.3 billion](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-scale-ai-15-billion-alexandr-wang-acquihire-ai-2025-6) on a 49% nonvoting stake in the company. Wang has been the chief AI officer of Meta since 2025.

## Jack Dorsey — cofounder and former CEO, Twitter; cofounder and CEO, Block

![Image 18: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dorsey is the CEO of Block. He was formerly the CEO of Twitter.Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc Nation Sports

Jack Dorsey first enrolled at the University of Missouri-Rolla, but he transferred to NYU after two years.

In a 2011 interview with [Wired](https://www.wired.com/2011/05/the-lost-origin-of-twitter/), Dorsey said he came up with the idea for Twitter while at NYU, where he dropped out a semester short of graduating in 1999. He moved to the West Coast to work for a tech company and pursued other interests outside tech.

Dorsey went on to cofound Twitter, now known as X, which launched in 2006. He stepped down as its CEO in 2021.

He cofounded the financial technology company Square, now known as Block, in 2009, and is currently its CEO.

## Evan Williams — cofounder and former CEO, Twitter

![Image 20: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Evan Williams is a venture capitalist.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Evan Williams grew up in a small town in Nebraska and enrolled at the nearby University of Nebraska-Lincoln, as reported by the [Omaha World-Herald.](https://omaha.com/news/nation-world/business/twitter-co-founder-evan-williams-success-doesn-t-surprise-those/article_5968322b-2c74-5c7a-97b8-414df1a8e413.html)

However, he told The New York Times in 2009 that he felt college was a "waste of time," and lasted only a year and a half.

Williams said in a 2009 [Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB124000817787330413) interview that he then moved to Florida and bounced around various cities, doing freelance work and tech jobs.

Like his fellow cofounder, Dorsey, Williams became a billionaire following Twitter's IPO. He is the cofounder of Obvious Ventures, a venture capital firm.

## Steve Jobs — cofounder and former CEO, Apple

![Image 22: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Steve Jobs cofounded Apple when he was 21.David Paul Morris/Getty Images

Steve Jobs attended Reed College in Portland, Oregon. The private university was "almost as expensive as Stanford," he said in a 2005 commencement speech at Stanford, adding, "I couldn't see the value in it."

"So I decided to drop out and trust that it would all work out OK," he said. "It was pretty scary at the time, but looking back, it was one of the best decisions I ever made."

[CNN](http://www.cnn.com/2011/TECH/innovation/08/25/steve.jobs.profile/index.html) reported that he dropped out after one semester, but he stayed in the area and attended classes that interested him.

One of those classes [was calligraphy](https://www.businessinsider.com/robert-palladino-calligraphy-class-inspired-steve-jobs-2016-3), taught by a Trappist monk named Robert Palladino, whom Jobs later credited with teaching him about typefaces that he added to the Mac personal computer he developed.

Jobs cofounded Apple in 1976 when he was 21.

## Jan Koum — cofounder and former CEO, WhatsApp

![Image 24: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jan Koum is an investor who cofounded WhatsApp.Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images for Discovery

[Jan Koum](https://www.businessinsider.com/whatsapp-ceo-jan-koum-rags-to-riches-2017-5) enrolled in San Jose State University while also working as a security tester at Ernst & Young.

While on assignment for EY, Koum was brought on to help at Yahoo, where[Forbes reported](https://www.forbes.com/sites/parmyolson/2014/02/19/exclusive-inside-story-how-jan-koum-built-whatsapp-into-facebooks-new-19-billion-baby/#64a125e02fa1) that he met an employee who would become his future WhatsApp cofounder, Brian Acton.

Koum switched jobs to become an infrastructure engineer at Yahoo, and was soon inundated with doing work on its servers.

He dropped out to devote his time to Yahoo, telling Forbes in 2014 that he "hated school anyway."

Koum and Acton left Yahoo in 2007 and cofounded WhatsApp in 2009. It was sold to Facebook for $19 billion in 2014.

## Dustin Moskovitz — cofounder, Facebook and Asana

![Image 26: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dustin Moskovitz dropped out of college to work on Facebook.Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Village Global

Dustin Moskovitz studied computer science at Harvard, where he was roommates with Mark Zuckerberg.

[Moskovitz volunteered](https://www.businessinsider.com/how-moskovitz-became-facebook-cofounder-2016-3) to help Zuckerberg work on his new website and learned a coding language in "a couple of days" to be able to work, according to a lecture Zuckerberg gave in 2005.

Along with Zuckerberg, [Moskovitz dropped out](https://www.businessinsider.com/how-facebook-was-founded-2010-3) of Harvard to move to Palo Alto and work on Facebook full-time.

He left Facebook in 2008 and cofounded Asana, a work management platform, where he was the CEO until 2025. He still serves as the chair of its board of directors.

## Travis Kalanick — cofounder and former CEO, Uber

![Image 28: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Kalanick was the CEO of Uber until 2017.Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

[Travis Kalanick](https://www.businessinsider.com/uber-travis-kalanick-bio-2014-1), a California native, enrolled in UCLA to study computer engineering.

Through the school's Computer Science Undergraduate Association, he met two classmates named Michael Todd and Vince Busam.

Kalanick worked with four other students out of Busam's dorm room to develop a peer-to-peer search engine called Scour.

He dropped out of school in 1998 to work for Scour full-time, and survived by collecting unemployment as the company looked to secure funding.

Kalanick cofounded Uber in 2009. He was the CEO until 2017.

## Arash Ferdowsi — cofounder, Dropbox

![Image 30: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Arash Ferdowsi at Dropbox's IPO in 2018.Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Arash Ferdowsi attended MIT, where he studied computer science and interned at Google as a software engineer for a summer.

In the summer of 2007, recent MIT graduate Drew Houston reached out to Ferdowsi to team up on an idea for a cloud storage service that later became Dropbox.

[Inc.](https://www.inc.com/30under30/2011/profile-drew-houston-and-arash-ferdowsi-founders-dropbox.html) reported in 2011 that Ferdowsi dropped out of MIT in his last semester to commit himself fully to Dropbox, and worked with Houston from a small office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to build the platform.

He is now a prominent business-to-business [startup investor](https://www.businessinsider.com/these-are-the-60-top-angel-investors-for-b2b-startups-2024-6).

## Michael Dell — founder and CEO, Dell

![Image 32: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Michael Dell has seen his wealth grow in 2026 amid AI-driven gains.Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images

[Entrepreneur](https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/197566) reported that Michael Dell attended the University of Texas in 1983 as a premed student, but by the end of his freshman year, he decided to drop out.

From his college dorm room, Dell founded the personal-computer company that would later become Dell. He [told Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/michael-dell-pivot-reinvention-interview-cloud-multicloud-2019-11) in 2019 that in the first nine months, the company's sales were $6 million, and the next year they were $33 million.

Forbes reported that as of 2026, Dell is the 13th [richest person](https://www.businessinsider.com/michael-dell-donald-trump-relationship-business-politics-2026-7) in the world with an estimated net worth of approximately $141 billion.

## Bill Gates — cofounder, Microsoft

![Image 34: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Bill Gates is a philanthropist and the cofounder of Microsoft.Bloomberg/Getty Images

[Bill Gates left Harvard](https://www.businessinsider.com/bill-gates-on-dropping-out-of-harvard-2016-10) in 1975 to cofound Microsoft with his childhood friend Paul Allen. In an obituary Gates wrote for Allen in The Wall Street Journal in 2018, Gates said they had decided on the new venture in December 1974.

When Gates left school, he took it as an official leave of absence. He said in a 1976 interview that he did so to allow him to return to school ["if things hadn't worked out."](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KJ4G1RtoKyI&t=53)

Gates was the CEO of Microsoft from 1975 to 2000. He is the chair of the Gates Foundation, a philanthropic organization, and has donated billions to charity.

## Paul Allen — cofounder, Microsoft

![Image 36: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Paul Allen launched Microsoft with childhood friend Bill Gates.Steve Dykes / Getty Images

The late Paul Allen dropped out of Washington State University in 1974 after two years to work as a programmer in Boston, where his friend since grade school — Bill Gates — was attending Harvard, [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2011/05/paul-allen-201105) reported.

The two childhood friends cofounded Microsoft. The BBC reported that Allen left Microsoft in 1983 after his first cancer diagnosis, but continued serving as a director.

## Shayne Coplan — founder and CEO, Polymarket

![Image 38: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Shayne Coplan is the founder and CEO of Polymarket Bloomberg/Getty Images

Shayne Coplan dropped out of New York University, where he was studying computer science, during his freshman year.

[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-08/polymarket-founder-is-youngest-self-made-billionaire-on-ice-deal) reported that he began exploring prediction markets and building Polymarket, a cryptocurrency-based prediction market that enables users to trade on the likelihood of future outcomes, such as election results and sports scores. It launched in 2020.

Bloomberg reported that in 2025, Intercontinental Exchange invested $2 billion in Polymarket, briefly making Coplan the world's youngest self-made billionaire at 27.

## Matt Mullenweg — founder and CEO, Automattic

![Image 40: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Matt Mullenweg cofounded WordPress.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Matt Mullenweg told the [Houston Press](https://www.houstonpress.com/news/the-blog-age-6574261/) in 2004 that he developed the open-source software for the blogging platform WordPress as a 19-year-old freshman at the University of Houston, where he was studying philosophy and political science.

By the start of his junior year, [he wrote](https://ma.tt/2004/10/press-and-cnet/) in a personal blog that he left college for a job at CNET in San Francisco.

He left the company in 2005, when he founded Automattic, which is behind WordPress.
