The debate around whether college is worth the [time and money](https://www.businessinsider.com/is-college-still-worth-it-tech-execs-kids-2026-5) has been heating up.

As AI reshapes what it means to be a white-collar worker, and amid [high tuition fees](https://www.businessinsider.com/most-expensive-colleges-tuition-in-us), some young people are rethinking the traditional path of [graduating from college](https://www.businessinsider.com/colleges-highest-earning-graduates-every-state) before entering the workforce.

By now, stories of [Mark Zuckerberg](https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg) and Bill Gates dropping out of college before earning their degrees have become tech-industry folklore. However, the Meta and Microsoft founders aren't the only influential executives who have risen to the top without finishing college.

The founders and CEOs of other tech companies — including [a new generation](https://www.businessinsider.com/gen-z-tech-founders-skipping-college-new-dropping-out-palantir-2025-6) of Gen Z AI talent — also left higher education to bet on the tech world.

Here are 21 tech executives who never got their college degrees.

## Mark Zuckerberg — founder and CEO, Meta

![Image 2: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Zuckerberg is pictured wearing the Ray-Ban Meta glasses.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Zuckerberg, founder and [CEO of Meta](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-launches-muse-spark-1-1-cost-effective-ai-2026-7), studied psychology and computer science at Harvard but left without completing a degree.

In 2004, while a student at Harvard University, he launched "thefacebook.com," which later became Facebook, but he dropped out during his sophomore year to move to Palo Alto and work on his company full-time.

"It's sort of been this taboo thing to say, maybe not everyone needs to go to college because there's, like, a lot of jobs that don't require that," [Zuckerberg told comedian Theo Von](https://www.businessinsider.com/mark-zuckerberg-theo-von-harvard-interview-2025-4) in a 2025 interview. "But I think people are probably coming around to that opinion a little more now than maybe like 10 years ago."

Zuckerberg received an honorary degree from Harvard in 2017.

## Sam Altman — cofounder and CEO, OpenAI

![Image 4: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Sam Altman said in an interview in 2025 that he's "envious" of the new generation of college dropouts.Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images

[Sam Altman studied computer science](https://www.businessinsider.com/sam-altman-openai-envies-college-dropouts-stanford-devday-2025-10) at Stanford University for two years before dropping out in 2005 at the age of 19.

He left to cofound location-sharing app Loopt, which was acquired in 2012 by Green Dot.

Altman became president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator in 2014. He [cofounded OpenAI](https://www.businessinsider.com/sam-altman) in 2015, alongside Elon Musk and other founders, and he became the CEO in 2019.

Altman said in an interview at the DevDay conference in 2025 that he is "envious of the current generation of 20-year-old dropouts."

"The amount of stuff you can build, the opportunity in this space is so incredibly wide," he said.

## John and Patrick Collison — cofounders, Stripe

![Image 6: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

John Collison (left) is the cofounder and president of Stripe, while his cofounder brother, Patrick Collison (right), is the CEO.Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Win McNamee/Getty Images

John and Patrick Collison grew up in Ireland. As teenagers, they hatched the idea for their first business, an online auction management company named Auctomatic.

The brothers sold Auctomatic in 2008 for $5 million, making them teen millionaires, [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2008/mar/27/technology.news) reported.

[Patrick Collison](https://www.businessinsider.com/the-stripe-ceo-floats-creating-software-on-demand-sell-off-2026-3) enrolled at MIT in 2006, but dropped out to work on his business ventures, while John Collison started at Harvard in 2009 and dropped out a year later to work on their new payments company, Stripe.

The brothers launched Stripe in 2010. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/24/stripe-value-stock-sale-tender-offer.html) reported that it was valued at $159 billion earlier this year.

## Mustafa Suleyman — CEO, Microsoft AI

![Image 8: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI.Stephen Brashear/Getty Images

Mustafa Suleyman grew up in London and studied philosophy and theology at Oxford University. He dropped out as the degree felt ["abstract and impractical"](https://www.businessinsider.com/mustafa-suleyman-the-lefty-activist-ensuring-google-deepmind-benefits-all-of-humanity-2017-12) to him.

After leaving university, Suleyman set up the Muslim Youth Helpline, a telephone counseling service, with a friend from university.

After working for several years in politics and consulting, Suleyman cofounded DeepMind in 2010.

In 2024, Suleyman became the executive vice president and CEO of the newly founded Microsoft AI.

## Melanie Perkins — cofounder and CEO, Canva

![Image 10: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Melanie Perkins is the cofounder and CEO of Canva.Nina Franova/Getty Images for SXSW Sydney

Melanie Perkins grew up in Perth, Australia, and attended the University of Western Australia, where she came up with the [idea of making design](https://apac.entrepreneur.com/women-entrepreneur/how-this-30-year-old-college-dropout-created-a-tech-unicorn/329883) easier, she told Entrepreneur in 2019.

Perkins launched [Fusion Books](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-42552367), a website that enables students to design their own yearbooks, with her then-boyfriend (and now-husband), Clifford Obrecht, in 2007.

She told the [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/business-42552367) that she decided to drop out of college, believing the concept could be applied to projects beyond yearbooks. Perkins began meeting investors in Silicon Valley in 2010.

In 2013, Perkins and Obrecht launched Canva. The company was valued at $42 billion in a 2025 employee share sale.

## Daniel Ek — cofounder and executive chair, Spotify

![Image 12: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Daniel Ek transitioned to the role of executive chair from CEO at the beginning of 2026.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Daniel Ek grew up in Sweden and enrolled at the country's KTH Royal Institute of Technology in 2002 to study engineering.

In an interview with [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevenbertoni/2012/01/04/spotifys-daniel-ek-the-most-important-man-in-music/#7cf824c664ca) in 2012, he said he lasted only eight weeks, when he found out his entire first year would be devoted to theoretical mathematics. He soon started taking gigs at various tech companies.

Ek cofounded Spotify in 2006, where he was the CEO until 2025. CNBC reported that he became a billionaire in 2018 when Spotify listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

## Larry Ellison — cofounder and CTO, Oracle

![Image 14: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Oracle cofounder Larry Ellison.[Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/oracle-co-founder-cto-and-executive-chairman-larry-ellison-news-photo/2197466221)

As a kid growing up in Chicago, [Larry Ellison](https://www.businessinsider.com/larry-ellison-shares-what-dropping-out-of-college-and-getting-divorced-taught-him-about-success-2016-5) planned to attend medical school at USC, get married and have kids, and move to Los Angeles to work as a doctor.

However, that never happened. [He tried to earn an undergraduate degree](https://www.businessinsider.com/rise-of-oracle-founder-larry-ellison-2017-1)twice: once at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (for two years) and again at the University of Chicago (where he lasted one semester).

After dropping out a second time, Ellison moved to California amid the burgeoning tech scene, where he cofounded what later became Oracle in 1977.

He now serves as the company's chief technology officer and, as of 2026, Forbes reported he remains one of the richest people in the world.

## Alexandr Wang — founder and former CEO, Scale AI; chief AI officer, Meta

![Image 16: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Alexandr Wang was named the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2021.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Born in Los Alamos, New Mexico, [Alexandr Wang](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-ai-model-catches-up-openai-gpt-5-says-2026-7) studied mathematics and computer science at MIT, according to his LinkedIn profile, before dropping out at 19 to launch Scale AI.

Forbes reported that Wang became the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2021, when he was 24. He held the title until he was overtaken by Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan in 2025.

He was the CEO of Scale AI until 2025, when [Meta spent roughly $14.3 billion](https://www.businessinsider.com/meta-scale-ai-15-billion-alexandr-wang-acquihire-ai-2025-6) on a 49% nonvoting stake in the company. Wang has been the chief AI officer of Meta since 2025.

## Jack Dorsey — cofounder and former CEO, Twitter; cofounder and CEO, Block

![Image 18: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dorsey is the CEO of Block. He was formerly the CEO of Twitter.Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc Nation Sports

Jack Dorsey first enrolled at the University of Missouri-Rolla, but he transferred to NYU after two years.

In a 2011 interview with [Wired](https://www.wired.com/2011/05/the-lost-origin-of-twitter/), Dorsey said he came up with the idea for Twitter while at NYU, where he dropped out a semester short of graduating in 1999. He moved to the West Coast to work for a tech company and pursued other interests outside tech.

Dorsey went on to cofound Twitter, now known as X, which launched in 2006. He stepped down as its CEO in 2021.

He cofounded the financial technology company Square, now known as Block, in 2009, and is currently its CEO.

## Evan Williams — cofounder and former CEO, Twitter

![Image 20: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Evan Williams is a venture capitalist.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Evan Williams grew up in a small town in Nebraska and enrolled at the nearby University of Nebraska-Lincoln, as reported by the [Omaha World-Herald.](https://omaha.com/news/nation-world/business/twitter-co-founder-evan-williams-success-doesn-t-surprise-those/article_5968322b-2c74-5c7a-97b8-414df1a8e413.html)

However, he told The New York Times in 2009 that he felt college was a "waste of time," and lasted only a year and a half.

Williams said in a 2009 [Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB124000817787330413) interview that he then moved to Florida and bounced around various cities, doing freelance work and tech jobs.

Like his fellow cofounder, Dorsey, Williams became a billionaire following Twitter's IPO. He is the cofounder of Obvious Ventures, a venture capital firm.

## Steve Jobs — cofounder and former CEO, Apple

![Image 22: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Steve Jobs cofounded Apple when he was 21.David Paul Morris/Getty Images

Steve Jobs attended Reed College in Portland, Oregon. The private university was "almost as expensive as Stanford," he said in a 2005 commencement speech at Stanford, adding, "I couldn't see the value in it."

"So I decided to drop out and trust that it would all work out OK," he said. "It was pretty scary at the time, but looking back, it was one of the best decisions I ever made."

[CNN](http://www.cnn.com/2011/TECH/innovation/08/25/steve.jobs.profile/index.html) reported that he dropped out after one semester, but he stayed in the area and attended classes that interested him.

One of those classes [was calligraphy](https://www.businessinsider.com/robert-palladino-calligraphy-class-inspired-steve-jobs-2016-3), taught by a Trappist monk named Robert Palladino, whom Jobs later credited with teaching him about typefaces that he added to the Mac personal computer he developed.

Jobs cofounded Apple in 1976 when he was 21.

## Jan Koum — cofounder and former CEO, WhatsApp

![Image 24: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jan Koum is an investor who cofounded WhatsApp.Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images for Discovery

[Jan Koum](https://www.businessinsider.com/whatsapp-ceo-jan-koum-rags-to-riches-2017-5) enrolled in San Jose State University while also working as a security tester at Ernst & Young.

While on assignment for EY, Koum was brought on to help at Yahoo, where[Forbes reported](https://www.forbes.com/sites/parmyolson/2014/02/19/exclusive-inside-story-how-jan-koum-built-whatsapp-into-facebooks-new-19-billion-baby/#64a125e02fa1) that he met an employee who would become his future WhatsApp cofounder, Brian Acton.

Koum switched jobs to become an infrastructure engineer at Yahoo, and was soon inundated with doing work on its servers.

He dropped out to devote his time to Yahoo, telling Forbes in 2014 that he "hated school anyway."

Koum and Acton left Yahoo in 2007 and cofounded WhatsApp in 2009. It was sold to Facebook for $19 billion in 2014.

## Dustin Moskovitz — cofounder, Facebook and Asana

![Image 26: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dustin Moskovitz dropped out of college to work on Facebook.Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Village Global

Dustin Moskovitz studied computer science at Harvard, where he was roommates with Mark Zuckerberg.

[Moskovitz volunteered](https://www.businessinsider.com/how-moskovitz-became-facebook-cofounder-2016-3) to help Zuckerberg work on his new website and learned a coding language in "a couple of days" to be able to work, according to a lecture Zuckerberg gave in 2005.

Along with Zuckerberg, [Moskovitz dropped out](https://www.businessinsider.com/how-facebook-was-founded-2010-3) of Harvard to move to Palo Alto and work on Facebook full-time.

He left Facebook in 2008 and cofounded Asana, a work management platform, where he was the CEO until 2025. He still serves as the chair of its board of directors.

## Travis Kalanick — cofounder and former CEO, Uber

![Image 28: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Kalanick was the CEO of Uber until 2017.Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

[Travis Kalanick](https://www.businessinsider.com/uber-travis-kalanick-bio-2014-1), a California native, enrolled in UCLA to study computer engineering.

Through the school's Computer Science Undergraduate Association, he met two classmates named Michael Todd and Vince Busam.

Kalanick worked with four other students out of Busam's dorm room to develop a peer-to-peer search engine called Scour.

He dropped out of school in 1998 to work for Scour full-time, and survived by collecting unemployment as the company looked to secure funding.

Kalanick cofounded Uber in 2009. He was the CEO until 2017.

## Arash Ferdowsi — cofounder, Dropbox

![Image 30: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Arash Ferdowsi at Dropbox's IPO in 2018.Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Arash Ferdowsi attended MIT, where he studied computer science and interned at Google as a software engineer for a summer.

In the summer of 2007, recent MIT graduate Drew Houston reached out to Ferdowsi to team up on an idea for a cloud storage service that later became Dropbox.

[Inc.](https://www.inc.com/30under30/2011/profile-drew-houston-and-arash-ferdowsi-founders-dropbox.html) reported in 2011 that Ferdowsi dropped out of MIT in his last semester to commit himself fully to Dropbox, and worked with Houston from a small office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to build the platform.

He is now a prominent business-to-business [startup investor](https://www.businessinsider.com/these-are-the-60-top-angel-investors-for-b2b-startups-2024-6).

## Michael Dell — founder and CEO, Dell

![Image 32: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Michael Dell has seen his wealth grow in 2026 amid AI-driven gains.Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images

[Entrepreneur](https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/197566) reported that Michael Dell attended the University of Texas in 1983 as a premed student, but by the end of his freshman year, he decided to drop out.

From his college dorm room, Dell founded the personal-computer company that would later become Dell. He [told Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/michael-dell-pivot-reinvention-interview-cloud-multicloud-2019-11) in 2019 that in the first nine months, the company's sales were $6 million, and the next year they were $33 million.

Forbes reported that as of 2026, Dell is the 13th [richest person](https://www.businessinsider.com/michael-dell-donald-trump-relationship-business-politics-2026-7) in the world with an estimated net worth of approximately $141 billion.

## Bill Gates — cofounder, Microsoft

![Image 34: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Bill Gates is a philanthropist and the cofounder of Microsoft.Bloomberg/Getty Images

[Bill Gates left Harvard](https://www.businessinsider.com/bill-gates-on-dropping-out-of-harvard-2016-10) in 1975 to cofound Microsoft with his childhood friend Paul Allen. In an obituary Gates wrote for Allen in The Wall Street Journal in 2018, Gates said they had decided on the new venture in December 1974.

When Gates left school, he took it as an official leave of absence. He said in a 1976 interview that he did so to allow him to return to school ["if things hadn't worked out."](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KJ4G1RtoKyI&t=53)

Gates was the CEO of Microsoft from 1975 to 2000. He is the chair of the Gates Foundation, a philanthropic organization, and has donated billions to charity.

## Paul Allen — cofounder, Microsoft

![Image 36: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Paul Allen launched Microsoft with childhood friend Bill Gates.Steve Dykes / Getty Images

The late Paul Allen dropped out of Washington State University in 1974 after two years to work as a programmer in Boston, where his friend since grade school — Bill Gates — was attending Harvard, [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2011/05/paul-allen-201105) reported.

The two childhood friends cofounded Microsoft. The BBC reported that Allen left Microsoft in 1983 after his first cancer diagnosis, but continued serving as a director.

## Shayne Coplan — founder and CEO, Polymarket

![Image 38: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Shayne Coplan is the founder and CEO of Polymarket Bloomberg/Getty Images

Shayne Coplan dropped out of New York University, where he was studying computer science, during his freshman year.

[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-08/polymarket-founder-is-youngest-self-made-billionaire-on-ice-deal) reported that he began exploring prediction markets and building Polymarket, a cryptocurrency-based prediction market that enables users to trade on the likelihood of future outcomes, such as election results and sports scores. It launched in 2020.

Bloomberg reported that in 2025, Intercontinental Exchange invested $2 billion in Polymarket, briefly making Coplan the world's youngest self-made billionaire at 27.

## Matt Mullenweg — founder and CEO, Automattic

![Image 40: Matt Mullenweg, founder and chief executive officer of Automattic, during TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Matt Mullenweg cofounded WordPress.Bloomberg/Getty Images

Matt Mullenweg told the [Houston Press](https://www.houstonpress.com/news/the-blog-age-6574261/) in 2004 that he developed the open-source software for the blogging platform WordPress as a 19-year-old freshman at the University of Houston, where he was studying philosophy and political science.

By the start of his junior year, [he wrote](https://ma.tt/2004/10/press-and-cnet/) in a personal blog that he left college for a job at CNET in San Francisco.

He left the company in 2005, when he founded Automattic, which is behind WordPress.

Business Insider is a leading global news brand renowned for its coverage of business, technology, and innovation, helping millions of readers get more out of their careers and lives through [award-winning journalism](https://www.businessinsider.com/awards).

Our journey began in 2007 when we burst onto the scene as Silicon Alley Insider. Two years later, we adopted the name Business Insider. We were trailblazers, breaking the real story of Facebook's founding, demystifying the 2008 financial crisis for our readers, and profiling the visionaries who built some of today's largest tech companies. We covered the startups and people our audience cared about, even if we occasionally ruffled some feathers. We showed the world that business journalism could be visual and fun.

Over time we grew into a global news organization, with journalists from New York to Singapore. We moved headquarters from a loading dock into a real office in the Financial District. We built a video team. We embraced social distribution and platforms. Our stories have changed government policies, gotten executives fired, launched investigations, and reopened closed cases. We turned small businesses into overnight sensations. We coined terms like "quiet quitting" that entered the zeitgeist. We tried lots of things — some ideas worked, others didn't. We won our first Pulitzer Prize.

Nearly two decades later, the core of who we are hasn't changed. Our [future as Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/note-from-business-insider-ceo-barbara-peng) reaffirms our commitment to business, tech, and innovation as our center of gravity.

with actual question constraints, and the next missing identifying fact. Original
page notes return separately. Preserve alternatives; repetition is not corroboration.
Do not invent facts, URLs or search requests. Missing evidence is not contradiction.

# Runways, rotors and whiskey: Raila’s time in the skies

 Thursday, October 23, 2025 Scroll down to read the article

Nasa leader Raila Odinga disembarks from the plane at JKIA on November 17, 2017.

Photo credit: File | Nation 

[![Image 4: Nation logo](https://zurl.co/resource/image/5062046/portrait_ratio1x1/60/60/d8283f00723c25684f90a39dbd341984/mR/nation-logo.jpg)](https://zurl.co/kenya/news/kamore-maina--4633514)

By[Kamore Maina](https://zurl.co/kenya/news/kamore-maina--4633514)

Correspondent

Nation Media Group

*   Related

He would stroll into the aircraft, donning that trademark smile and eyes fixed on the seats closest to the cockpit.

After isolating where to sit for the flight, Raila Amolo Odinga would then settle down and exchange pleasantries with the pilot, Raphael Wamwati, and any other members of the crew present.

By the time Wamwati would have achieved a cruising altitude of 35,000 feet, Raila would most likely be holding a glass tumbler, marvelling at the skies while asking his pilot all sorts of aviation-related questions.

![Image 5: Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati raila](https://zurl.co/resource/image/5242460/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/80bf4c958cd0b9ed063f7f57d4907e21/mG/captain-raphael-sebastian-wamwati-photo.jpg)

Twinstar Aviation Managing Partner Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati.

The contents of the tumbler would depend on his mood. At times, it was the single malt scotch whiskey, Glenfiddich. Other times it was the blended scotch whiskey, Johnnie Walker.

Read:[_**Military gun salute and fly-past for Raila Odinga, a man who ruled without occupying seat of power**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/military-gun-salute-and-fly-past-for-raila-odinga-a-man-who-ruled-without-occupying-seat-of-power-5237092)

But whichever way Raila’s decision swung, the liquid gold sipped in the sky had most likely spent more than 18 years maturing in an oak cask.

And Raila would sip from the tumbler as he also gulped from Wamwati’s well of knowledge.

He loved the skies but was fascinated by the workings of aircraft and would never shy away from asking anything aviation for the duration of the flight.

That was Raila, the passenger in the eyes of Wamwati, who spent several hundred hours in the skies with the former Premier.

Some trips were for political excursions, others for business dealings, and others for private affairs like family trips.

For 13 years, Raila was a repeat client at Twinstar Aviation. Wamwati was on many of those flights as the captain.

“He loved flying. He loved being in an aircraft and was always keen for details while inside airplanes. He would watch closely as we navigated the airspace to the different destinations that we travelled to. You could tell he had an interest in aviation from the many questions that he asked,” Wamwati said in an exclusive interview with the _Nation_ at Wilson Airport, Nairobi.

Having enjoyed the company of Raila and his family in the skies for the last 13 years, Wamwati describes the ex-Prime Minister as one of the most interesting clients that he has handled in his 22-year career in the aviation industry.

Read:[_**Raila the brand: The 10 things that defined ex-premier and drove his supporters wild**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/raila-brand-10-things-defined-ex-premier-drove-supporters-wild-5235532)

## Most interesting clients

Wamwati and Twinstar Aviation Executive Chairman Dr Richard Kubo have flown several VIPs, local and foreign, through Kenya’s airspace for over two decades, with some becoming friends.

They maintain that Raila is one of the most interesting clients.

![Image 6: DnRailaPilot2210k](https://zurl.co/resource/image/5241188/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/9518af860d1520c1aa9362aa3b85e036/JY/dnrailapilot2210k.jpg)

Dr Richard Kubo, Executive Chairman of Twinstar Aviation (left), and Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati, Managing Partner, both flew the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga on several political, business and private trips. They were interviewed at the Twinstar Aviation offices in Wilson Airport, Nairobi, on October 22, 2025.

Photo credit: Bonface Bogita | Nation

On August 26, 2024, a convoy of state-of-the-art sports utility vehicles chauffeured Raila and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo from the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) to Wilson Airport.

The two revered African statesmen were to catch a flight to Kisumu, where they were among VIP attendants of the Festac Festival – an event celebrating the diversity in various cultural showcases like music, dance and storytelling.

Their friendship, forged at the graveside of Kenya’s first Vice-President and Raila’s father, Jaramogi Oginga Odinga, stood the test of time. Much like his aggressive and shrewd politics, Raila inherited a friend from his father in Obasanjo.

Many a time, Obasanjo was in Kenya to stand with Raila and the Odinga family at large.

In 1994, he was there to condole with the Odingas’ loss of Jaramogi. He was there for the anniversary of Jaramogi’s death a year later. He was there for the opening of the East African Spectre plant off Mombasa road in 1995.

When Raila and then President Mwai Kibaki could not see eye-to-eye on the outcome of the 2007 presidential election, Obasanjo was among many continental leaders trying to broker a deal.

Read:[_**Raila: Why Kondele has refused to move on**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/counties/kisumu/raila-why-kondele-has-refused-to-move-on-5239404)

At the peak of a bitter rivalry which had Raila and President William Ruto feuding on opposite sides in 2023, Obasanjo reprised his heart softener role and got the two talking.

![Image 7](https://zurl.co/resource/image/4526446/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/ac273f068798e16f77e67d85d7ca4bcf/bd/ruto-obasanjo1.jpg)

Former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo meeting with President William Ruto on February 15 2024.

That ceasefire, arguably, conceived the Broad-based union of President Ruto’s Kenya Kwanza coalition and Raila’s ODM party barely a year later.

On many of those occasions, Raila and Obasanjo flew around Kenya aboard a Twinstar Aviation aircraft, piloted by Wamwati.

Last Sunday, Obasanjo, Wamwati and Kubo were there to help write the final chapter in the book that is Raila Amolo Odinga’s book – to bury a man who successfully juggled politics, business and family even as successive governments threw everything but the kitchen sink in an attempt to solve the “problem” that was Raila.

At Wilson Airport in August 2024, the Twinstar crew waited patiently to fly the two buddies to the Kisumu International Airport on a chartered aircraft.

An officer from the Foreign Affairs ministry had received Raila and Obasanjo, and was there to execute the usual protocol whenever such dignitaries are moving around, and handle the logistics.

The Foreign Affairs officer announced that there were two aircraft, one for each of the VIPs. Such individuals are never to fly in the same aircraft, as a crash would mean maximum loss.

But Raila was never one to follow protocol. It was protocol to be bent to his whims.

Kubo said that Raila was insistent on travelling with Obasanjo.

“The officer said that Raila and Obasajo could not fly together in the same plane. He explained that owing to their VIP status, the protocol demanded that they fly separate in the event of an incident. Raila told the protocol officer with a firm look on his face; These are my boys. I know them very well and nothing will happen,” Wamwati said in the interview at Twinstar’s Wilson Airport offices.

Read:[_**Jowi! Jowi! Origin and meaning of Raila’s famous dirge**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/jowi-jowi-origin-and-meaning-5235536)

![Image 8: Raila Odinga and Olusegun Obasanjo](https://zurl.co/resource/image/4526132/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/c5d9ffb016a9965650c702b102292ce5/Bc/raila-obasanjo.jpg)

Azimio la Umoja leader Raila Odinga with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo in Nairobi on February 15, 2024 when he formally declared interest in the African Union Commission chairmanship.

Photo credit: Lucy Wanjiru | Nation Media Group

Eventually, the protocol officer gave in and allowed Raila and Obasajo to board the same aircraft to Kisumu, where they both attended the FESTAC festival.

“They (Obasanjo and Raila) were all smiles as we landed in Kisumu,” recalled Kubo, stressing that the former Prime Minister loved to fly.

For Raila, defying protocol may have been something he did every other day.

But for Wamwati, that defiance made August 26, 2024, one of the few that remain etched in his memory.

When the _Nation_ visited their offices at Wilson Business within the Langata aerodrome, Wamwati and Kubo had flown back from Kisumu International Airport.

They were among the chosen few who attended Raila’s burial at Kang’o ka Jaramogi in Siaya County.

Wamwati and Kubo were going through several photographs that they took with Raila over the years.

Read:[_**Raila Odinga's death end of moral bloodline**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/blogs-opinion/opinion/raila-odinga-s-death-end-of-moral-bloodline-5240442)

![Image 9](https://zurl.co/resource/image/679220/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/2709dbaaf4791bcf75a0a1c345585da3/vt/dnodingahosp2906.jpg)

Fidel Odinga arrives at the Nairobi Hospital on June 29, 2010 to visit his father.

Photo credit: File | Nation

Wamwati revealed that he and Kubo were first introduced to the Odinga family by Raila’s firstborn, Fidel Odinga, in 2007.

They became close friends, with the latter doubling up as a loyal client of Twinstar Aviation.

“Our relationship moved from the friendship with Fidel to a more robust relationship of friends and business people,” said Kubo.

Raila may have rested, but for the Twinstar crew, the former Prime Minister lives through the many memories made in the skies and which forged a new friendship for the pilot.

# Runways, rotors and whiskey: Raila’s time in the skies

He would stroll into the aircraft, donning that trademark smile and eyes fixed on the seats closest to the cockpit.

After isolating where to sit for the flight, Raila Amolo Odinga would then settle down and exchange pleasantries with the pilot, Raphael Wamwati, and any other members of the crew present.

By the time Wamwati would have achieved a cruising altitude of 35,000 feet, Raila would most likely be holding a glass tumbler, marvelling at the skies while asking his pilot all sorts of aviation-related questions.

![Image 5: Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati raila](https://zurl.co/resource/image/5242460/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/80bf4c958cd0b9ed063f7f57d4907e21/mG/captain-raphael-sebastian-wamwati-photo.jpg)

Twinstar Aviation Managing Partner Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati.

The contents of the tumbler would depend on his mood. At times, it was the single malt scotch whiskey, Glenfiddich. Other times it was the blended scotch whiskey, Johnnie Walker.

Read:[_**Military gun salute and fly-past for Raila Odinga, a man who ruled without occupying seat of power**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/military-gun-salute-and-fly-past-for-raila-odinga-a-man-who-ruled-without-occupying-seat-of-power-5237092)

But whichever way Raila’s decision swung, the liquid gold sipped in the sky had most likely spent more than 18 years maturing in an oak cask.

And Raila would sip from the tumbler as he also gulped from Wamwati’s well of knowledge.

He loved the skies but was fascinated by the workings of aircraft and would never shy away from asking anything aviation for the duration of the flight.

That was Raila, the passenger in the eyes of Wamwati, who spent several hundred hours in the skies with the former Premier.

Some trips were for political excursions, others for business dealings, and others for private affairs like family trips.

For 13 years, Raila was a repeat client at Twinstar Aviation. Wamwati was on many of those flights as the captain.

“He loved flying. He loved being in an aircraft and was always keen for details while inside airplanes. He would watch closely as we navigated the airspace to the different destinations that we travelled to. You could tell he had an interest in aviation from the many questions that he asked,” Wamwati said in an exclusive interview with the _Nation_ at Wilson Airport, Nairobi.

Having enjoyed the company of Raila and his family in the skies for the last 13 years, Wamwati describes the ex-Prime Minister as one of the most interesting clients that he has handled in his 22-year career in the aviation industry.

Read:[_**Raila the brand: The 10 things that defined ex-premier and drove his supporters wild**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/raila-brand-10-things-defined-ex-premier-drove-supporters-wild-5235532)

## Most interesting clients

Wamwati and Twinstar Aviation Executive Chairman Dr Richard Kubo have flown several VIPs, local and foreign, through Kenya’s airspace for over two decades, with some becoming friends.

They maintain that Raila is one of the most interesting clients.

![Image 6: DnRailaPilot2210k](https://zurl.co/resource/image/5241188/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/9518af860d1520c1aa9362aa3b85e036/JY/dnrailapilot2210k.jpg)

Dr Richard Kubo, Executive Chairman of Twinstar Aviation (left), and Captain Raphael Sebastian Wamwati, Managing Partner, both flew the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga on several political, business and private trips. They were interviewed at the Twinstar Aviation offices in Wilson Airport, Nairobi, on October 22, 2025.

Photo credit: Bonface Bogita | Nation

On August 26, 2024, a convoy of state-of-the-art sports utility vehicles chauffeured Raila and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo from the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) to Wilson Airport.

The two revered African statesmen were to catch a flight to Kisumu, where they were among VIP attendants of the Festac Festival – an event celebrating the diversity in various cultural showcases like music, dance and storytelling.

Their friendship, forged at the graveside of Kenya’s first Vice-President and Raila’s father, Jaramogi Oginga Odinga, stood the test of time. Much like his aggressive and shrewd politics, Raila inherited a friend from his father in Obasanjo.

Many a time, Obasanjo was in Kenya to stand with Raila and the Odinga family at large.

In 1994, he was there to condole with the Odingas’ loss of Jaramogi. He was there for the anniversary of Jaramogi’s death a year later. He was there for the opening of the East African Spectre plant off Mombasa road in 1995.

When Raila and then President Mwai Kibaki could not see eye-to-eye on the outcome of the 2007 presidential election, Obasanjo was among many continental leaders trying to broker a deal.

Read:[_**Raila: Why Kondele has refused to move on**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/counties/kisumu/raila-why-kondele-has-refused-to-move-on-5239404)

At the peak of a bitter rivalry which had Raila and President William Ruto feuding on opposite sides in 2023, Obasanjo reprised his heart softener role and got the two talking.

![Image 7](https://zurl.co/resource/image/4526446/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/ac273f068798e16f77e67d85d7ca4bcf/bd/ruto-obasanjo1.jpg)

Former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo meeting with President William Ruto on February 15 2024.

That ceasefire, arguably, conceived the Broad-based union of President Ruto’s Kenya Kwanza coalition and Raila’s ODM party barely a year later.

On many of those occasions, Raila and Obasanjo flew around Kenya aboard a Twinstar Aviation aircraft, piloted by Wamwati.

Last Sunday, Obasanjo, Wamwati and Kubo were there to help write the final chapter in the book that is Raila Amolo Odinga’s book – to bury a man who successfully juggled politics, business and family even as successive governments threw everything but the kitchen sink in an attempt to solve the “problem” that was Raila.

At Wilson Airport in August 2024, the Twinstar crew waited patiently to fly the two buddies to the Kisumu International Airport on a chartered aircraft.

An officer from the Foreign Affairs ministry had received Raila and Obasanjo, and was there to execute the usual protocol whenever such dignitaries are moving around, and handle the logistics.

The Foreign Affairs officer announced that there were two aircraft, one for each of the VIPs. Such individuals are never to fly in the same aircraft, as a crash would mean maximum loss.

But Raila was never one to follow protocol. It was protocol to be bent to his whims.

Kubo said that Raila was insistent on travelling with Obasanjo.

“The officer said that Raila and Obasajo could not fly together in the same plane. He explained that owing to their VIP status, the protocol demanded that they fly separate in the event of an incident. Raila told the protocol officer with a firm look on his face; These are my boys. I know them very well and nothing will happen,” Wamwati said in the interview at Twinstar’s Wilson Airport offices.

Read:[_**Jowi! Jowi! Origin and meaning of Raila’s famous dirge**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/jowi-jowi-origin-and-meaning-5235536)

![Image 8: Raila Odinga and Olusegun Obasanjo](https://zurl.co/resource/image/4526132/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/c5d9ffb016a9965650c702b102292ce5/Bc/raila-obasanjo.jpg)

Azimio la Umoja leader Raila Odinga with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo in Nairobi on February 15, 2024 when he formally declared interest in the African Union Commission chairmanship.

Photo credit: Lucy Wanjiru | Nation Media Group

Eventually, the protocol officer gave in and allowed Raila and Obasajo to board the same aircraft to Kisumu, where they both attended the FESTAC festival.

“They (Obasanjo and Raila) were all smiles as we landed in Kisumu,” recalled Kubo, stressing that the former Prime Minister loved to fly.

For Raila, defying protocol may have been something he did every other day.

But for Wamwati, that defiance made August 26, 2024, one of the few that remain etched in his memory.

When the _Nation_ visited their offices at Wilson Business within the Langata aerodrome, Wamwati and Kubo had flown back from Kisumu International Airport.

They were among the chosen few who attended Raila’s burial at Kang’o ka Jaramogi in Siaya County.

Wamwati and Kubo were going through several photographs that they took with Raila over the years.

Read:[_**Raila Odinga's death end of moral bloodline**_](https://nation.africa/kenya/blogs-opinion/opinion/raila-odinga-s-death-end-of-moral-bloodline-5240442)

![Image 9](https://zurl.co/resource/image/679220/landscape_ratio2x1/320/160/2709dbaaf4791bcf75a0a1c345585da3/vt/dnodingahosp2906.jpg)

Fidel Odinga arrives at the Nairobi Hospital on June 29, 2010 to visit his father.

Photo credit: File | Nation

Wamwati revealed that he and Kubo were first introduced to the Odinga family by Raila’s firstborn, Fidel Odinga, in 2007.

They became close friends, with the latter doubling up as a loyal client of Twinstar Aviation.

**Arianna Stassinopoulos Huffington** ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")**Ariadnē-Anna Stasinopoúlou**; [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"): Αριάδνη-Άννα Στασινοπούλου, pronounced[[ariˈaðni ˈana stasinoˈpulu]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Greek "Help:IPA/Greek"); born July 15, 1950) is a Greek and American author, [syndicated columnist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicated_columnist "Syndicated columnist") and businesswoman.

She is a co-founder of _[HuffPost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HuffPost "HuffPost")_, the founder and CEO of [Thrive Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrive_Global "Thrive Global"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:1-1) and the author of fifteen books.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-2) She has been named in [_Time_ magazine's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)") list of the world's 100 most influential people[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Forbes2020-3) and the _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ Most Powerful Women list.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:2-4) Huffington serves on numerous boards, including [Onex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onex_Corporation "Onex Corporation") and Global Citizen.

Two of her books have been dogged by allegations of [plagiarism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagiarism "Plagiarism"), for one of which she paid another author an out-of-court settlement. Her last two books, _Thrive: The Third Metric to Redefining Success and Creating a Life of Well-Being, Wisdom, and Wonder_ and _The Sleep Revolution: Transforming Your Life, One Night at a Time_, both became international bestsellers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-5)

Huffington, the former wife of Republican congressman [Michael Huffington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Huffington "Michael Huffington"), co-founded _[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Huffington\_Post "The Huffington Post")_, which was later acquired by [BuzzFeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuzzFeed "BuzzFeed").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-6) She was a popular [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") commentator in the mid-1990s, after which, in the late 1990s, she offered [liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_liberalism_in_the_United_States "Modern liberalism in the United States") points of view in public, while remaining involved in business endeavors.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-7) In 2003, she ran as an [independent candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_candidate "Independent candidate") for [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_California "Governor of California") in the [California recall election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_California_recall_election "2003 California recall election") and lost.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-8) In 2009, Huffington was No.12 in _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ first-ever list of the Most Influential Women In Media.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-9) She has also moved up to No.42 in _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s Top 100 in Media List.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-10) As of 2014, she was listed by _Forbes_ as the 52nd Most Powerful Woman in the World.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-11) She had moved to 77th as of 2018 and dropped off the list as of 2019.

In 2011, [AOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL "AOL") acquired _The Huffington Post_ for US$315 million and made Huffington the president and [editor-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Editor-in-chief "Editor-in-chief") of The Huffington Post Media Group, which included _The Huffington Post_ and then-existing AOL properties including [AOL Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL_Music "AOL Music"), [Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget"), [Patch Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patch_Media "Patch Media"), and StyleList.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-AOL_Press_Release-12)

She stepped down from her role at _The Huffington Post_ in August 2016 to focus on a new start-up, [Thrive Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrive_Global "Thrive Global"), a behavior-change technology company with the mission of improving productivity and health outcomes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-13)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Huffington was born Ariadnē-Anna Stasinopoúlou (Αριάδνη-Άννα Στασινοπούλου) in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), Greece,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:2-4) in 1950,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-14) the daughter of Konstantinos (a journalist and management consultant) and Elli (née Georgiadi) Stasinopoulou,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-yaya/19990222-15) and is the sister of Agapi (an author, speaker, and performer).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Silverman-16) She moved to the United Kingdom at the age of 16 and studied [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics") at [Girton College, Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girton_College,_Cambridge "Girton College, Cambridge"), where she was the first foreign, and third female,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Talbot,_Margaret_1998_page_40-47-17)[president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Cambridge_Union_Society_presidents "List of Cambridge Union Society presidents") of the [Cambridge Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Union "Cambridge Union").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-18) She studied abroad in India, and told IANS in an email interview "India has long held a special place in my heart, from the time I went to study comparative religion at [Visva-Bharati University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visva-Bharati_University "Visva-Bharati University")."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-19)

In 1971, Huffington appeared in an edition of _[Face the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face\_the\_Music\_(UK\_TV\_programme) "Face the Music (UK TV programme)")_ along with [Bernard Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Levin "Bernard Levin"). A relationship developed, of which she wrote, after his death: "He wasn't just the big love of my life, he was a mentor as a writer and a role model as a thinker."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-arianna-20) Huffington began writing books in the 1970s, with editorial help from Levin.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-22) The two traveled to music festivals around the world for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"). They spent summers patronizing three-star restaurants in France. At the age of 30, she remained deeply in love with him but longed to have children; Levin never wanted to marry or have children.

From March to April 1980, Huffington joined [Bob Langley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Langley "Bob Langley") as the co-host of [BBC1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC1 "BBC1")'s late-night talk and entertainment show _Saturday Night at the Mill_, appearing in just five editions before being dropped from the programme.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-23)

In 1973, Arianna (as Stasinopoúlou) wrote a book titled _The Female Woman_, attacking the Women's Liberation movement in general and [Germaine Greer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germaine_Greer "Germaine Greer")'s 1970 _[The Female Eunuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Female\_Eunuch "The Female Eunuch")_ in particular. In the book she wrote, "Women's Lib claims that the achievement of total liberation would transform the lives of all women for the better; the truth is that it would transform only the lives of women with strong lesbian tendencies."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:3-24)

In the late 1980s, Huffington wrote several articles for _[National Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Review "National Review")_. In 1981, she wrote a biography of [Maria Callas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Callas "Maria Callas"), _Maria Callas – The Woman Behind the Legend_, and in 1989, a biography of [Pablo Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Picasso "Pablo Picasso"), _Picasso: Creator and Destroyer_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-25)

Huffington rose to the national U.S. prominence during the unsuccessful Senate bid in 1994 by her then husband, Michael Huffington, a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). She became known as a reliable supporter of conservative causes such as [Newt Gingrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich "Newt Gingrich")'s "[Republican Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Revolution "Republican Revolution")" and [Bob Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dole "Bob Dole")'s 1996 [candidacy for president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_presidential_election "1996 United States presidential election"). She teamed up with [liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism "Liberalism")[comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedian "Comedian")[Al Franken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Franken "Al Franken") as the conservative half of "Strange Bedfellows"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-26) during [Comedy Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Central "Comedy Central")'s coverage of the 1996 U.S. presidential election. For her work, she and the writing team of _[Politically Incorrect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politically\_Incorrect "Politically Incorrect")_ were nominated for a 1997 [Emmy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy "Emmy") for Outstanding Writing for a Variety or Music Program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-27)

As late as 1998, Huffington still aligned herself with the Republican Party. During that year, she did a weekly radio show in Los Angeles called _[Left, Right & Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left,\_Right\_&\_Center "Left, Right & Center")_, that "match[ed] her, the so-called 'right-winger', against self-described centrist policy wonk [Matt Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Miller_(journalist) "Matthew Miller (journalist)"), and veteran 'leftist' journalist [Robert Scheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Scheer "Robert Scheer")."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Talbot,_Margaret_1998_page_40-47-17)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-28) In an April 1998 profile in _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_, [Margaret Talbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Talbot "Margaret Talbot") wrote, "Most recently, she has cast herself as a kind of Republican Spice Girl – an endearingly ditzy right wing gal-about-town who is a guilty pleasure for people who know better." Huffington described herself by side-stepping the traditional party divide, saying "the right–left divisions are so outdated now. For me, the primary division is between people who are aware of what I call 'the two nations' (rich and poor), and those who are not."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Talbot,_Margaret_1998_page_40-47-17)

Huffington, of Greek background, opposed the [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") intervention in [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") during the [Yugoslav Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_Wars "Yugoslav Wars")[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-29) and in 2000, she co-convened the "Shadow Conventions",[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-30) which appeared at the [Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Republican_National_Convention "2000 Republican National Convention") in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") and the [Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Democratic_National_Convention "2000 Democratic National Convention") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") at [Patriotic Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Patriotic_Hall "Bob Hope Patriotic Hall").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-31)

Campaigning for [Governor of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_California "Governor of California"), 2003

Huffington headed [The Detroit Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Detroit_Project "The Detroit Project"), a public interest group [lobbying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobbying "Lobbying") automakers to start producing cars running on [alternative fuels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_fuel "Alternative fuel"). The project's 2003 TV ads, which equated driving [sport utility vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_utility_vehicle "Sport utility vehicle") to funding [terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorism "Terrorism"), proved to be particularly controversial, with some stations refusing to run them.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-32)

In a 2004 appearance on _[The Daily Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Show "The Daily Show")_ with [Jon Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stewart "Jon Stewart"), she announced her endorsement of [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") by saying, "When your house is burning down, you don't worry about the remodeling."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-33) Huffington was a panel speaker during the 2005 California Democratic Party State Convention, held in Los Angeles. She also spoke at the 2004 [College Democrats of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Democrats_of_America "College Democrats of America") Convention in Boston, which was held in conjunction with the [2004 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Democratic_National_Convention "2004 Democratic National Convention"). She was also a regular panelist on the nationally syndicated weekend radio program, _Both Sides Now with Huffington & Matalin_,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-bothsides-34) hosted by [Mark Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Green_(New_York_politician) "Mark Green (New York politician)").

Huffington serves on the board of directors of the [Berggruen Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berggruen_Institute "Berggruen Institute"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-35) the [Center for Public Integrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Public_Integrity "Center for Public Integrity"),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-36)[Uber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-37) and [Onex Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onex_Corporation "Onex Corporation").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-38)

She is also a One Young World Counsellor, speaking to delegates at summits in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), in 2013 and [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland "Republic of Ireland"), in 2014. She spoke about her "third metric" for success and the value of youth leadership.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-39)

On May 22, 2016, she gave the commencement address[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-40) and received an [honorary degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_degree "Honorary degree") from [Colby College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colby_College "Colby College") in Waterville, Maine.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-41) Also in 2016, she was named to [Oprah Winfrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oprah_Winfrey "Oprah Winfrey")'s _SuperSoul100_ list of visionaries and influential leaders.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-42)

Huffington has authored 15 books in her career. She faced 37 rejections before securing a publishing contract for her second book. Huffington also wrote the foreword for Marina Khidekel's book 'Your Time to Thrive,' published in 2021.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-44)

### _The Huffington Post_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Huffington Post")]

In 2005, Huffington founded _[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HuffPost "HuffPost")_ (now known as _HuffPost_) with[Andrew Breitbart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Breitbart "Andrew Breitbart"), [Kenneth Lerer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Lerer "Kenneth Lerer"), and [Jonah Peretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Peretti "Jonah Peretti").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-46) It was launched on May 9, 2005, as a commentary outlet, blog, and an alternative to news aggregators such as the _[Drudge Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drudge\_Report "Drudge Report")_. The site historically published work from both paid staff writers and reporters and unpaid bloggers.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-47) In February 2011, [AOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL "AOL") acquired _The Huffington Post_ for US$315 million, making Huffington editor-in-chief of The Huffington Post Media Group.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-48) In 2012, _The Huffington Post_ became the first commercially run United States digital media enterprise to win a [Pulitzer Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize "Pulitzer Prize").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-49) In 2016, Huffington left _The Huffington Post_.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-huffingtongone-50)

### Thrive Global

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Thrive Global")]

Main article: [Thrive Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrive_Global "Thrive Global")

In 2016 Huffington stepped down from her positions at AOL and _Huffington Post_ to launch her new enterprise, Thrive Global, which claims to offer "science-based solutions" to end stress and burnout.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-51)

*   **Meditative Story Podcast** – In August 2019, Thrive Global launched the podcast [Meditative Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meditative_Story "Meditative Story") in partnership with WaitWhat – a media company led by former TED executives [June Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Cohen "June Cohen") and Deron Triff. The podcast supposedly combines first-person stories with meditation prompts and original music to create a "mindfulness experience" in audio.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-52)_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ has described it as "part first-person narrative podcast and part guided meditation."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-53)_Forbes_ has described it as "a completely new kind of listening experience that blends intimate first-person stories with mindfulness prompts, enveloped in beautiful music composition."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:0-54) Huffington described Meditative Story as "a response to a deep cultural need in our hyper sped up world to have a moment to recharge. The podcast is a tool-set for wellness combining intimate storytelling, that we’re all hardwired to respond to, plus moments of reflection."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:0-54) The podcast's first season featured stories from [Krista Tippett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krista_Tippett "Krista Tippett") (host of the radio show [On Being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Being "On Being")), NPR Host [Peter Sagal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Sagal "Peter Sagal"), travel writer [Pico Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pico_Iyer "Pico Iyer"), LinkedIn cofounder [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman"), Beautycon Media's [Moj Mahdara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moj_Mahdara "Moj Mahdara"), actor [Josh Radnor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Radnor "Josh Radnor"), and astronomer [Michelle Thaller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Thaller "Michelle Thaller"), among others.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-55)
*   **Thrive Global Podcast** – In 2017, Thrive Global launched a podcast with iHeart Radio featuring Huffington as host.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-56)

### California recall election participation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: California recall election participation")]

Huffington was an [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_independent "Political independent") candidate in the [2003 California gubernatorial recall election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_California_gubernatorial_recall_election "2003 California gubernatorial recall election") of California Governor [Gray Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray_Davis "Gray Davis"). She described her candidacy against frontrunner [Arnold Schwarzenegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Schwarzenegger "Arnold Schwarzenegger") as "the [hybrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_car "Hybrid car") versus the [Hummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hummer "Hummer")", making reference to her ownership of a hybrid vehicle, the [Toyota Prius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Prius "Toyota Prius"), and Schwarzenegger's Hummer. The two would proceed to have a high-profile clash during the election's [debate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debate "Debate").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-57)

She dropped out of the race on September 30, 2003, and endorsed Governor Gray Davis' campaign to vote against the recall. Polls showed that only about 2 percent of California voters planned to vote for her at the time of her withdrawal.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-58) In the announcement of her withdrawal, Huffington stated,

> "It has become clear to me that the only way to stop a Republican takeover of our state is to vote No on the recall. Because it's also clear that I am not going to win on October 7, I am withdrawing from the race so that I can devote all my time and energy in the remaining week to defeating the recall – and to defeating the Arnold Schwarzenegger-[Pete Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Wilson "Pete Wilson") forces that are trying to use the recall to hijack our state."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-59)

Though she failed to stop the recall, Huffington's name remained on the ballot and she [placed 5th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_California_recall_election#Results "2003 California recall election"), capturing 47,505 votes – less than 1% of the vote.

### Presence in media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Presence in media")]

Huffington was a panelist on the weekly [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4") political discussion programme _[Any Questions?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Any\_Questions%3F "Any Questions?")_, and the BBC television panel games _[Call My Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_My\_Bluff\_(UK\_game\_show) "Call My Bluff (UK game show)")_ and _[Face the Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face\_the\_Music\_(UK\_TV\_programme) "Face the Music (UK TV programme)")_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-60) She served as co-host of BBC's late-night chat show _Saturday Night at the Mill_ for four weeks before viewer complaints caused her to be dropped from the show.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-61) Huffington at one point was the co-host of the weekly, nationally syndicated [public radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_radio "Public radio") program _Both Sides Now_, along with [Mary Matalin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Matalin "Mary Matalin"), former top aide to the [George W. Bush administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_George_W._Bush "Presidency of George W. Bush"). Every week on _Both Sides Now_, Huffington and Matalin discussed the nation's relevant political issues, offering both sides of every issue to listeners. _Both Sides Now_ was hosted by former [Air America Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_America_Radio "Air America Radio") president and _HuffPost_ blogger [Mark Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Green_(New_York_politician) "Mark Green (New York politician)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-bothsides-34)

Prior to _The Huffington Post_, Huffington hosted a website called AriannaOnline.com. Her first foray onto the internet was a website called Resignation.com, which called for the resignation of President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and was a rallying place for conservatives opposing Clinton. About Clinton resigning, she wrote, "Only some act of sacrifice can begin to restore the image of the President that we are left with from the [Starr report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starr_report "Starr report") – a man of staggering [narcissism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narcissism "Narcissism") and self-indulgence, whom nobody dared gainsay, investing his energies first in gratifying his sexual greeds and then in using his staff, his friends, and the Secret Service to cover up the truth."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-62)

In November 2008, Huffington joined the cast of [Seth MacFarlane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane "Seth MacFarlane")'s animated series _[The Cleveland Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cleveland\_Show "The Cleveland Show")_, where she lent her voice to the wife of [Tim the Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_the_Bear "Tim the Bear"), also named [Arianna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_Cleveland_Show_characters#Arianna_the_Bear "List of The Cleveland Show characters").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-63)

Huffington participated in the 24th annual "Distinguished Speaker Series" at the [University at Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_at_Buffalo "University at Buffalo"), New York, on September 16, 2010. ## Claims of plagiarism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Claims of plagiarism")]

Huffington was accused of [plagiarism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagiarism "Plagiarism") for copying material for her book _Maria Callas_ (1981); the claims were settled out of court in 1981, with Callas' biographer Gerald Fitzgerald being paid "in the low five figures."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Orth,_Maureen_2005_Page_117-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-70)

## Religious views

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Religious views")]

Huffington has had a lifelong interest in spirituality; in her youth, together with Bernard Levin, she explored the [Rajneesh movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajneesh_movement "Rajneesh movement"), later dating [Erhard Seminars Training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erhard_Seminars_Training "Erhard Seminars Training") founder [Werner Erhard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Erhard "Werner Erhard") and going on to become affiliated with [John-Roger Hinkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John-Roger_Hinkins "John-Roger Hinkins")' [Movement of Spiritual Inner Awareness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movement_of_Spiritual_Inner_Awareness "Movement of Spiritual Inner Awareness").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:3-24)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-71) In 1994, she published a self-help book titled _The Fourth Instinct_, outlining her view that people should rise above the three basic instincts of survival, power, and sex to find their higher and better selves.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-vanessa-g-nymag-72)

## Awards and honors

Huffington was named to the 2011 Time 100 as a media mogul.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-73) Huffington was selected for the inaugural 2021 [Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") 50 Over 50; made up of entrepreneurs, leaders, scientists and creators who are over the age of 50.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-74)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arianna_Huffington&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Huffington is Greek by birth[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-vanessa-g-nymag-72) and became a [naturalized American citizen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalized_American_citizen "Naturalized American citizen") in 1990.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-75) She met her husband [Michael Huffington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Huffington "Michael Huffington") in 1985.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-76) They were married a year later, on April 12, 1986,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-77) and have two daughters.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-78)

The couple later moved to [Santa Barbara, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California"), and, in 1992, Michael ran as a Republican for a seat in the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives"), winning the election by a significant margin. In 1994, he [narrowly lost the race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_United_States_Senate_election_in_California "1994 United States Senate election in California") for the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") seat in California to incumbent [Dianne Feinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein "Dianne Feinstein").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-79)

The couple divorced in 1997.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-80) In 1998, Michael Huffington shared that he was [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual "Bisexual"), saying, "I know now that my sexuality is part of who I am, I've been through a long process of finding out the truth about me."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-82) He stated, "In December 1985, in my Houston townhouse I sat down with [Arianna] and told her that I had dated women and men so that she would be aware of it... The good news was that it was not an issue for her."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-:3-24)

Huffington has residences in New York City, with her sister, Agapi Stassinopoulos,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-Silverman-16) and the [Brentwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentwood,_Los_Angeles "Brentwood, Los Angeles") neighborhood of Los Angeles.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Huffington#cite_note-85)
